title.en: Volume 276 Biographies 63: Shi Lin, Xu Chao, Bei Henuo, Bo Ji, Jiang Chenxi, Liu Yinshu, Yin Tai, E Hai, Wei Jiqi
title.raw: 卷276 列傳六十三 石琳 徐潮 贝和诺 博霁 蒋陈锡 刘荫枢 音泰 鄂海 卫既齐

sentences.zh: 列傳六十三

translations.literal: Biographies 63
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 63

sentences.zh: 石琳兄子文晟徐潮子杞貝和諾子馬喇陶岱

translations.literal: Shi Lin; his nephew Wencheng; Xu Chao; his son Ziqi; Bei Henuo; his son Mala; Tao Dai
translations.idiomatic: Shi Lin; his nephew Wencheng; Xu Chao; his son Ziqi; Bei Henuo; his son Mala; Tao Dai

sentences.zh: 傅霽覺羅華顯蔣陳錫子漣泂劉廕樞

translations.literal: Bo Ji; Aisin Gioro Hua Xian; Jiang Chenxi; his sons Lian and Jiong; Liu Yinshu
translations.idiomatic: Bo Ji; Aisin Gioro Hua Xian; Jiang Chenxi; his sons Lian and Jiong; Liu Yinshu

sentences.zh: 音泰鄂海衛既齊

translations.literal: Yin Tai; E Hai; Wei Jiqi
translations.idiomatic: Yin Tai; E Hai; and Wei Jiqi

sentences.zh: 石琳，漢軍正白旗人，石廷柱第四子。

translations.literal: Shi Lin was a man of the Han Eight Banners' Plain White Banner, the fourth son of Shi Tingzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Lin, of the Han military Plain White Banner, was the fourth son of Shi Tingzhu.

sentences.zh: 初授佐領，兼禮部郎中。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed as an assistant commandant and concurrently served as a director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He began as an assistant commandant while also holding a directorship in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，出為山東按浙江鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, he was sent out to Shandong as surveillance commissioner and [served as] Zhejiang salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 (1662), he was posted to Shandong as provincial surveillance commissioner and appointed Zhejiang salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十二年，轉湖廣下荊南道。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was transferred to the Lower Jingnan Circuit in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1673 he was transferred to the Lower Jingnan circuit in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 十三年，襄陽總兵楊來喜、副將洪福以南漳叛應吳三桂，據房縣、保康、竹山。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Xiangyang garrison commander Yang Laixi and vice-commander Hong Fu rebelled at Nanzhang in support of Wu Sangui and seized Fang, Baokang, and Zhushan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1674 the Xiangyang commander Yang Laixi and his deputy Hong Fu rose at Nanzhang for Wu Sangui and occupied Fang, Baokang, and Zhushan.

sentences.zh: 琳偕總兵劉成龍率師討之，撫定各峒寨。

translations.literal: Lin together with garrison commander Liu Chenglong led troops to suppress them and pacified the various stockade villages.
translations.idiomatic: Lin joined Garrison Commander Liu Chenglong in a punitive campaign and brought the stockade settlements back under control.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷河南按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was promoted to Henan provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1676 he was promoted to Henan surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 禁旅南征，牧馬開封，當麥秋，琳與統兵諸將帥約，令兵毋驛騷，坐帳中四十餘日。

translations.literal: The Forbidden Troops marched south and pastured horses at Kaifeng during the wheat harvest. Lin made an agreement with the various commanders that the soldiers should not disturb the courier stations, and he sat in his tent for more than forty days.
translations.idiomatic: When the metropolitan banners marched south and grazed their horses at Kaifeng at harvest time, Lin secured a pledge from the field commanders that troops would not harass the countryside; he kept watch in his tent for over forty days.

sentences.zh: 及去，民得穫麥。

translations.literal: When they departed, the people were able to harvest the wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the troops left could the farmers bring in their wheat.

sentences.zh: 二十年，遷浙江布政使。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he was transferred to Zhejiang provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1681 he became Zhejiang administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時耿精忠初平，衢州被兵尤甚，戶口逃亡，丁賦皆責之里甲。

translations.literal: At that time Geng Jingzhong had just been pacified; Quzhou had suffered warfare most severely, the population had fled, and corvée levies were all charged to the village headmen.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong had only just been subdued; Quzhou had borne the brunt of the fighting, people had fled, and corvée quotas were still being forced onto village headmen.

sentences.zh: 琳覈實，請免之。

translations.literal: Lin verified the facts and requested exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Lin audited the registers and petitioned for relief.

sentences.zh: 師行供億浩繁，民多逋負，琳悉為釐定，裁革陋規，禁加耗尤嚴。

translations.literal: Military campaigns required vast supplies; the people owed much in arrears. Lin put everything in order, cut abusive practices, and was especially strict in forbidding surcharges.
translations.idiomatic: Army logistics had piled up enormous demands and arrears were widespread; Lin reorganized the levies, abolished corrupt local fees, and rigorously banned grain surcharges.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「革一分火耗，可增一分正供。

translations.literal: He once said: "Eliminate one part of the melting loss surcharge and you can increase the regular quota by one part."
translations.idiomatic: He once remarked, "Cut one measure of the melting-loss surcharge and you add one measure to the lawful tax."

sentences.zh: 」二十三年，擢湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-third year he was promoted to Hubei governor.
translations.idiomatic: " In 1684 he was promoted to governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 工部以修建太和殿，檄各省採柟、杉諸木。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Works, for the construction of the Hall of Supreme Harmony, ordered each province to procure nanmu, fir, and other timbers.
translations.idiomatic: The Works Ministry, rebuilding the Hall of Supreme Harmony, requisitioned nanmu and fir timber from every province.

sentences.zh: 琳言柟產萬山中，挽運甚艱，請寬其程限。

translations.literal: Lin stated that nanmu grew deep in the mountains and transport was extremely difficult, and requested an extension of the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Lin argued that nanmu came from remote mountains and haulage was punishingly hard, and asked that the deadline be relaxed.

sentences.zh: 部議不許。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberation did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry rejected the request.

sentences.zh: 特詔允之。

translations.literal: A special edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a special edict approving it.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，調雲南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1686 he was transferred to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「詳覈賦役全書，應更改者八事。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Upon detailed verification of the complete register of taxes and corvée, eight matters ought to be revised."
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "A thorough review of the tax-and-corvée register shows eight items that should be changed."

sentences.zh: 雲南自明初置鎮設衛，以田養軍曰屯田。

translations.literal: Since the early Ming, Yunnan established garrisons and guards; fields used to support troops were called garrison farms.
translations.idiomatic: From early Ming times Yunnan had garrison commands and military colonies whose fields supported the troops.

sentences.zh: 又有給指揮等官為俸，聽其招佃者曰官田。

translations.literal: There were also lands granted to commanders and other officers as salary, which they were allowed to lease out—these were called official fields.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders and other officers also held salary lands they could lease to tenants, known as official fields.

sentences.zh: 其租入較民賦十數倍，猶佃民之納租於田主。

translations.literal: Their rents were ten-odd times higher than civilian land tax, like tenants paying rent to a landlord.
translations.idiomatic: Rents ran more than ten times the civilian rate, much like tenant payments to a landlord.

sentences.zh: 國初吳三桂留鎮，以租額為賦額，相沿至今，積逋愈多，官民交困。

translations.literal: At the beginning of our dynasty Wu Sangui remained in command and made the rent quota the tax quota; this has continued to the present, arrears have piled ever higher, and officials and people alike are distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty Wu Sangui kept the garrison and treated rent as tax; the practice lingered, arrears mounted, and both government and populace suffered.

sentences.zh: 宜改依民賦上則起科。

translations.literal: It is fitting to change and assess according to the upper grade of civilian land tax.
translations.idiomatic: They should be reassessed at the top civilian land-tax rate instead.

sentences.zh: 雲南鹽井有九，以各井行鹽之多寡為每歲徵課之重輕。

translations.literal: Yunnan has nine salt wells; the annual levy's weight or lightness was set according to how much salt each well marketed.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan's nine salt wells were taxed each year in proportion to their output.

sentences.zh: 瑯井鹽斤徵課六釐，白井八釐，至黑井則倍。

translations.literal: Lang Well levied six cash per jin of salt, Bai Well eight cash, while Hei Well was double.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Well paid six cash per jin, Bai Well eight, and Hei Well twice as much.

sentences.zh: 明末加徵，較明初原額不啻數倍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming additional levies were imposed, several times the original quota of the early Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Late-Ming surcharges had raised rates many times above the early-Ming base.

sentences.zh: 今請減黑、白二井之課如瑯井例。

translations.literal: Now it is requested to reduce the levies on Hei and Bai wells to follow the Lang Well precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He now asks that Hei and Bai wells be cut back to Lang Well's rate.

sentences.zh: 開化民田畝科糧二斗六升三合，較未設府以前加至十倍。

translations.literal: Civilian fields in Kaihua were assessed two dou, six sheng, and three he of grain per mu—ten times what they were before the prefecture was established.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihua's civilian land was taxed at 2.633 dou of grain per mu, ten times the pre-prefecture rate.

sentences.zh: 通省民糧，惟河陽最重，今當減半，與河陽一例。

translations.literal: Among the province's civilian grain taxes, only Heyang was heaviest; now it should be halved to match Heyang's rate.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang bore the heaviest civilian grain levy in the province; it should now be halved and aligned with Heyang's standard.

sentences.zh: 元江由土改流，三桂於額糧外別立名色：曰田地講銀，曰茶商稅銀，曰普洱無耗秋米，曰浪媽等六寨地租。

translations.literal: Yuanjiang was converted from native to regular administration; beyond the quota grain Sangui created separate items: field discussion silver, tea merchant tax silver, Pu'er unreduced autumn grain, and land rent for Langma and five other stockades.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanjiang was brought under direct rule, Sangui added surcharges beyond the quota: field-negotiation silver, tea-merchant tax, Pu'er autumn grain without deduction, and rents for Langma and five other stockades.

sentences.zh: 加賦倍徵，民不堪命，應請各減其半。

translations.literal: Additional levies were doubled; the people could not bear it—each should be reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: Doubled exactions had crushed the people; each item should be cut by half.

sentences.zh: 通海六寨地糧較民賦重幾三倍，當改依新定民賦科則。

translations.literal: Grain tax on the six stockades of Tonghai was several times heavier than civilian tax; it should be changed to follow the newly fixed civilian assessment scale.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghai's six stockades paid several times the civilian rate and should be brought under the new civilian schedule.

sentences.zh: 咢嘉每糧一石，徵條編銀四兩有奇，亦為偏重。

translations.literal: For each shi of grain at Ejia, more than four taels of silver under the consolidated levy were collected—also excessively heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Ejia collected over four taels of consolidated-levy silver per shi of grain—another excessive burden.

sentences.zh: 今既歸南安州附徵，應與州賦一律，每糧一石，徵銀一兩四分。

translations.literal: Now that it has been attached to Nan'an Prefecture for collection, it should follow the prefectural rate: for each shi of grain, one tael and four fen of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Now subsumed under Nan'an Prefecture, it should pay the prefectural rate of 1.4 taels per shi.

sentences.zh: 麗江界連土番，古稱荒服。

translations.literal: Lijiang bordered native tribes; in antiquity it was called the wild frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Lijiang bordered tribal lands long counted as the wild frontier.

sentences.zh: 三桂叛後，割金沙江以內喇普地與蒙番，地去而糧存，當刪除。

translations.literal: After Sangui's rebellion, lands within the Jinsha River at Lapa were ceded to the Meng tribes; the territory was gone but the grain quota remained—it should be deleted.
translations.idiomatic: After Sangui's revolt, Lapa lands west of the Jinsha were given to Meng tribes; the land was lost but the tax remained and should be struck.

sentences.zh: 建水自明時設參將，歲派村寨陋規銀三百有奇、糧八十餘石，三桂遂編入正額，當裁革。

translations.literal: Since the Ming, Jianshui had a deputy commander; each year more than three hundred taels of abusive village fees and over eighty shi of grain were assigned—Sangui then entered them into the regular quota and they should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Jianshui's Ming-era deputy command had imposed over 300 taels of village fees and 80 shi of grain yearly; Sangui made them statutory and they should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 新平之銀場，易門之銅廠，礦斷山空，宜盡豁課稅。

translations.literal: The silver mines of Xinping and copper works of Yimen—the ore was exhausted and the mountains empty; all levies should be fully remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xinping's silver pits and Yimen's copper works were worked out; their taxes should be forgiven entirely.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，下所司議，刊入全書頒行。

translations.literal: " When the memorial arrived, it was sent down to the relevant offices for deliberation and published in the complete register for promulgation.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was referred to the ministries, adopted, and entered into the official tax register.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，擢兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was promoted to governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1689 he was made governor-general of the two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 瓊州總兵吳啟爵奏瓊屬黎地，請設州縣，築城垣，增兵防守。

translations.literal: Qiongzhou garrison commander Wu Qijue memorialized on Li territory subordinate to Qiong, requesting establishment of prefectures and counties, construction of walls, and increased troops for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Qiongzhou Commander Wu Qijue asked to convert Li lands under Qiong into regular counties, build walls, and station more troops.

sentences.zh: 命琳勘奏，力陳其非要，上從之。

translations.literal: Lin was ordered to investigate and report; he strongly stated its impropriety, and the emperor followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Lin investigate; Lin argued forcefully against the plan, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，連州瑤作亂，遣都統嵩祝等會剿，平之。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year the Yao of Lianzhou rebelled; he dispatched banner general Song Zhu and others for joint suppression and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1702 the Lianzhou Yao rose; Lin sent Banner General Song Zhu and others to suppress them successfully.

sentences.zh: 琳規畫善後，定官吏管轄，撥兵移防，悉協機宜。

translations.literal: Lin planned the aftermath, fixed civil and military jurisdiction, redeployed troops for defense—all suited to circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Lin arranged postwar administration, defined jurisdictions, and shifted garrisons—all to good effect.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒官。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office.

sentences.zh: 兄子文晟，初授薊州同知，歷雲南開化、山西平陽知府。

translations.literal: His nephew Wencheng was first appointed subprefect of Jizhou, and successively served as prefect of Kaihua in Yunnan and Pingyang in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Wencheng began as Jizhou subprefect and later governed Kaihua in Yunnan and Pingyang in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十三年，上嘉其居官有聲，超擢貴州布政使。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year of Kangxi the emperor praised his reputation in office and promoted him out of turn to Guizhou provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1694 the emperor noted his strong record and leapfrogged him to Guizhou administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是歲，即遷雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: That same year he was immediately transferred to Yunnan governor.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he became Yunnan governor.

sentences.zh: 為政務舉大綱。

translations.literal: In governing he attended to the great outlines.
translations.idiomatic: He governed by focusing on essentials rather than minutiae.

sentences.zh: 雲南屯賦科重民田數倍，琳官巡撫時，奏減而未議行；

translations.literal: Yunnan's garrison-farm tax was several times heavier than civilian fields; when Lin was governor he memorialized for reduction but it was not yet implemented;
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan garrison farms were taxed several times the civilian rate; Lin had petitioned for cuts as governor, but the court had not acted;

sentences.zh: 文晟复疏請，特允減舊額十之六。

translations.literal: Wencheng again memorialized requesting it; a special approval granted reduction of six-tenths of the old quota.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng renewed the petition, and the emperor specially approved cutting the old quota by sixty percent.

sentences.zh: 安南國王黎維疏告國內牛羊、蝴蝶、普園三地為鄰界土司侵占，乞敕諭歸還。

translations.literal: The king of Annam, Li Wei, memorialized that within his country the three places Niuyang, Hudie, and Puyuan had been seized by neighboring native chiefs, and begged an imperial order for their return.
translations.idiomatic: Annam's King Li Wei reported that Niuyang, Hudie, and Puyuan had been seized by neighboring native chiefs and asked the court to order their return.

sentences.zh: 會文晟入覲，上問文晟，奏言：「此地明時即內屬，非安南地。

translations.literal: When Wencheng came to audience, the emperor questioned Wencheng, who replied: "These places were already inner territory in Ming times and are not Annamese land."
translations.idiomatic: When Wencheng attended court, the emperor asked him; he replied, "Those places were imperial territory under the Ming—not Annam's."

sentences.zh: 妄言擅奏，不宜允。

translations.literal: To speak rashly and memorialize on one's own authority should not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: His claim was presumptuous and should be denied.

sentences.zh: 」乃降詔切責之。

translations.literal: " An edict was then issued sternly rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: " The court sent a sharp edict of rebuke.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，調廣東。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1704 he was transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，擢湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1705 he became Huguang governor-general.

sentences.zh: 坐劾容美土司田舜年僭妄淫虐非實，部議當降調，上命留任。

translations.literal: He was impeached for charging Rongmei native chieftain Tian Shunnian with presumption and debauchery that were not factual; the ministry deliberation called for demotion, but the emperor ordered him retained.
translations.idiomatic: He was censured for falsely accusing Rongmei chieftain Tian Shunnian of arrogance and cruelty; the ministry recommended demotion, but the emperor kept him in post.

sentences.zh: 文晟以疾乞退，上諭大學士曰：「文晟粗鄙，若為土司事而罷，似未得體。

translations.literal: Wencheng begged to retire on grounds of illness; the emperor instructed the grand secretaries: "Wencheng is coarse and uncouth; if he were dismissed over the native chieftain affair, it would seem improper."
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng sought retirement on grounds of illness; the emperor told the grand secretaries, "Wencheng is rough-edged; dismissing him over the chieftain case would look petty."

sentences.zh: 今既引疾，可允其請。

translations.literal: Now that he has cited illness, his request may be granted."
translations.idiomatic: Since he pleads illness, let him go."

sentences.zh: 」罷歸。

translations.literal: " He was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1720.

sentences.zh: 徐潮，字青來，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Xu Chao, style name Qinglai, was a native of Qiantang, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chao (Qinglai), from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討，累擢少詹事。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the twelfth year of Kangxi, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed reviser, and successively promoted to junior tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1673, entered the Hanlin Academy, became a reviser, and rose to junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 潮學問淹通，在翰林，應奉文字，多出其手。

translations.literal: Chao's learning was broad and penetrating; in the Hanlin, most of the compositions for imperial service came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar of wide learning, he drafted most of the court's ceremonial writings in the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 聖祖嘗禦門召講易、論語，敷陳明晰，為之傾聽。

translations.literal: The Sacred Ancestor once summoned him at the palace gate to lecture on the Changes and the Analects; his exposition was clear, and the emperor listened with full attention.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi once had him lecture on the Changes and Analects at the palace gate; the emperor listened closely to his lucid exposition.

sentences.zh: 三遷至工部侍郎，督理錢局，清介不苟隨俗。

translations.literal: After three promotions he reached vice minister of Works, supervised the mint, and was upright and incorruptible, not compromising with custom.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted thrice, he became vice minister of Works, oversaw the mint, and maintained a scrupulous independence.

sentences.zh: 局官冒濫事發，潮獨無所連染。

translations.literal: When abuses by mint officials came to light, Chao alone was not implicated.
translations.idiomatic: When the mint scandal broke, Chao alone was untouched.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，典會試。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1694 he served as chief examiner of the metropolitan civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 以母憂歸，服闋，起刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He returned home for mourning his mother; when the mourning period ended, he was recalled as vice minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he returned as vice minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，授河南巡撫，上諭之曰：「河南火耗最重，州縣多虧欠，爾當籌畫禁止。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was appointed Henan governor; the emperor instructed him: "Henan's melting-loss surcharge is heaviest and prefectures and counties owe much in arrears—you must plan to forbid it."
translations.idiomatic: In 1700 he became Henan governor; the emperor told him, "Henan's melting-loss surcharges are the worst in the empire and counties are deep in debt—you must stop it."

sentences.zh: 」潮上官，令火耗無過一分，州縣私派，悉皆禁革。

translations.literal: " When Chao took up his post, he ordered that melting loss should not exceed one percent and abolished all private levies by prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he capped melting loss at one percent and abolished every unauthorized local levy.

sentences.zh: 南陽承解黑鉛，衛輝辦兌漕米，向皆假手胥吏，恣為侵漁。

translations.literal: Nanyang's delivery of black lead and Weihui's handling of tribute-grain conversion had always been left to clerks, who preyed on the people at will.
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang's lead deliveries and Weihui's grain conversions had long been farmed out to clerks who extorted the populace.

sentences.zh: 潮悉心區畫，宿弊悉除。

translations.literal: Chao carefully planned each matter and removed all longstanding abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Chao reorganized both operations and cleared away entrenched corruption.

sentences.zh: 開封五府飢，疏請漕糧暫徵改折，以平市直。

translations.literal: When the five prefectures around Kaifeng suffered famine, he memorialized requesting temporary conversion of grain tribute collection to cash payment to stabilize market prices.
translations.idiomatic: During famine in the five Kaifeng prefectures he asked to collect tribute grain in cash to steady prices.

sentences.zh: 歸德屬永城、虞城、夏邑三縣被災地畝至一萬七千餘頃，出糶常平、義、社倉穀，借給貧民牛種，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: In Guide, Yongcheng, Yucheng, and Xiayi of the three counties had disaster-affected fields reaching more than seventeen thousand qing; he released grain from Ever-Normal, charity, and community granaries for sale, and lent oxen and seed to poor households—very many were preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: More than 17,000 qing were hit in Yongcheng, Yucheng, and Xiayi under Guide; he sold grain from government granaries and lent cattle and seed to the poor, saving countless lives.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，上巡幸畿甸，問巡撫李光地鄰省督撫賢否，光地舉潮對。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, when the emperor toured the capital region, he asked Governor Li Guangdi whether neighboring governors and governors-general were worthy; Guangdi named Chao in reply.
translations.idiomatic: On his 1702 tour of the capital region the emperor asked Li Guangdi which neighboring governors were capable; Li named Chao.

sentences.zh: 上褒美，以潮與光地、張鵬翮、彭鵬、郭琇並​​稱。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him and ranked Chao together with Guangdi, Zhang Penghe, Peng Peng, and Guo Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him, naming Chao alongside Guangdi, Zhang Penghe, Peng Peng, and Guo Xiu as model officials.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，上南巡，潮迎​​駕泰安，賜冠服及御書榜額。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, when the emperor toured south, Chao met the imperial procession at Tai'an and was granted court robes and an imperially inscribed plaque.
translations.idiomatic: During the 1703 southern tour Chao met the emperor at Tai'an and received court dress and an imperial plaque.

sentences.zh: 其冬，西巡，复迎駕，賞賚有加。

translations.literal: That winter, on the western tour, he again met the imperial procession and received additional rewards.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, on the western tour, he again met the emperor and received further gifts.

sentences.zh: 上念汾、渭皆入河，議於河南儲穀，遇山、陝歲歉，自水道移粟，便於陸運。

translations.literal: The emperor reflected that the Fen and Wei both enter the Yellow River and proposed storing grain in Henan so that when Shanxi and Shaanxi had lean years, grain could be moved by waterway, easier than overland transport.
translations.idiomatic: Noting that the Fen and Wei flow into the Yellow River, the emperor proposed grain reserves in Henan so Shanxi and Shaanxi could be fed by water rather than costly land transport in lean years.

sentences.zh: 命潮會陝西、山西督撫勘議。

translations.literal: Chao was ordered to meet with the governors-general and governors of Shaanxi and Shanxi to survey and deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was told to confer with the Shaanxi and Shanxi governors on the plan.

sentences.zh: 潮與川陝總督博霽會勘三門砥柱。

translations.literal: Chao together with Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general Bo Ji jointly surveyed the pillar rocks at Sanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Chao and Sichuan-Shaanxi Governor-General Bo Ji inspected the Sanmen Gorge rapids together.

sentences.zh: 語見博霽傳。

translations.literal: The account appears in Bo Ji's biography.
translations.idiomatic: See Bo Ji's biography for details.

sentences.zh: 又別疏言：「汴水通淮，一自中牟東經祥符至宿遷，湮塞已久；

translations.literal: He also separately memorialized: "The Bian River connects to the Huai—one route from east of Zhongmou through Xiangfu to Suqian has long been silted shut;
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he wrote: "The Bian once reached the Huai: one channel east from Zhongmou through Xiangfu to Suqian has been blocked for ages;

sentences.zh: 一自中牟東南經尉氏至太和，今名賈魯河，尚可通流：請量加疏濬。

translations.literal: another from southeast of Zhongmou through Weishi to Taihe, now called the Jia-Lu River, can still flow—please dredge it as appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: another southeast from Zhongmou through Weishi to Taihe—the present Jia-Lu River—still runs and should be dredged."

sentences.zh: 鄭州北別有支河，舊跡尚存，若於此建閘，使汴與洛通，尤為民便。

translations.literal: North of Zhengzhou there is another branch river whose old course still exists; if a sluice were built here to connect the Bian and Luo, it would especially benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: A branch north of Zhengzhou still shows its old bed; a sluice there linking the Bian and Luo would greatly help the people.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，擢戶部尚書，充經筵講官，兼翰林院掌院學士，教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was promoted to minister of Revenue, served as lecturer at the classics colloquium, and concurrently as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy instructing Hanlin bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: In 1704 he became minister of Revenue, lectured at the classics colloquium, and headed the Hanlin Academy as tutor to new bachelors.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，扈從南巡，命赴河南按事。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he accompanied the southern tour and was ordered to go to Henan to investigate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1705 he joined the southern tour and was sent back to Henan on an investigative mission.

sentences.zh: 時上以高郵、寶應諸州縣頻年被水患，由洪澤湖無所宣洩，宜於高堰二壩築堤束水入河，又於下河築堤束水入海。

translations.literal: At that time, because Gaoyou, Baoying, and other prefectures and counties had suffered flooding year after year, since Hongze Lake had no outlet for discharge, dikes should be built at the two dams of Gaoyan to channel water into the river, and dikes built on the lower river to channel water into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyou and Baoying had flooded repeatedly because Hongze Lake had no outlet; the emperor wanted dikes at Gaoyan's two dams to drive water into the river and lower-river dikes to send it to the sea.

sentences.zh: 會潮按事還，上詢河壖形勢，因指授方略，命往董其役。

translations.literal: When Chao returned from his investigation, the emperor inquired about the river-bank situation, personally instructed strategy, and ordered him to go oversee the work.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao returned, the emperor asked about the levees, outlined his plan, and put Chao in charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，監修高家堰滾水壩、高郵車邏中壩，並濬文華寺減河。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he supervised repair of the Gaojiayan spillway dam, the Gaoyou Cheluo central dam, and dredging of the Wenhua Temple diversion canal.
translations.idiomatic: In 1706 he oversaw the Gaojiayan spillway, Gaoyou's Cheluo middle dam, and dredging of the Wenhua Temple relief channel.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，監修武家壩、天然壩、蔣家壩及諸堤閘，先後畢工。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, he supervised repairs to the Wujia Dam, Tianran Dam, Jiangjia Dam, and various dikes and sluices; the work was completed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year he oversaw reconstruction of the Wujia, Tianran, and Jiangjia dams and other dikes and sluice gates, finishing each project in turn.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year, he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，以病乞休，許以原官致仕。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, on grounds of illness he requested retirement; he was permitted to retire with his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year he asked to retire on account of illness and was allowed to leave office at his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, he died; the court granted sacrificial rites and funeral honors.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifty-fourth year, and the court bestowed state funeral rites upon him.

sentences.zh: 潮居官平易，不事矯飾，所至民咸稱頌。

translations.literal: Chao in office was easygoing and unpretentious, not given to affectation; wherever he went the people all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: As an official Xu Chao was plain and unpretentious, and the people everywhere he served spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，追諡文敬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign, he was posthumously given the temple name Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign he was posthumously honored with the title Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 子本，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Ben has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ben is the subject of a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 杞，字集功。

translations.literal: Qi, styled Jigong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi, styled Jigong.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十一年進士，官編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fifty-first year of Kangxi; he served as a compiler in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifty-first year of Kangxi and served as a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 由甘肅布政使巡撫陝西，入為宗人府府丞。

translations.literal: From Gansu provincial treasurer he became governor of Shaanxi; he then entered the capital as vice-director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as Gansu treasurer and governor of Shaanxi, he was recalled to the capital as vice-director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 予休致，卒。

translations.literal: He was granted retirement, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from office and later died.

sentences.zh: 貝和諾，富察氏，滿洲正黃旗人，濟席哈孫。

translations.literal: Bei Henuo, of the Fuca clan, a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner, a descendant of Jixihasun.
translations.idiomatic: Bei Henuo, a Manchu of the Fuca clan in the Plain Yellow Banner and a descendant of Jixihasun.

sentences.zh: 自工部筆帖式授戶部主事，歷郎中，兼佐領，累遷大理寺卿。

translations.literal: Starting as a clerk in the Ministry of Works, he was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, served as a department director, concurrently held a company captaincy, and was repeatedly promoted to president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from a clerk in the Ministry of Works to secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, then department director and company captain, and was eventually promoted to president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十五年，命往山東經理閘河。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi, he was ordered to go to Shandong to manage the sluice canal.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi he was sent to Shandong to oversee the sluice canal.

sentences.zh: 漕運總督桑額奏漕船盡過濟寧，較往歲早一月。

translations.literal: Grand Canal transport governor Sang'e memorialized that all grain barges had passed Jining, a full month earlier than in previous years.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Canal transport governor Sang'e reported that all grain barges had cleared Jining a month ahead of previous years.

sentences.zh: 上以遣官經理，於漕運便，命以為常。

translations.literal: The emperor considered that dispatching an official to manage the work made grain transport more convenient, and ordered that this become regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decided that sending an official to manage the canal benefited grain transport and made the arrangement permanent.

sentences.zh: 遷左副都御史，擢戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to left vice censor-in-chief and promoted to vice president of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left vice censor-in-chief and then promoted to vice president of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，朝鮮歲祲，國王李焞乞開市義州中江貿穀。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, Korea suffered a bad harvest; King Yi Sun requested that a market be opened at Uiju on the Yalu River to trade for grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year famine struck Korea, and King Yi Sun asked permission to open a market at Uiju on the Yalu River to buy grain.

sentences.zh: 詔發三萬石與為市，令貝和諾及侍郎陶岱監視。

translations.literal: An edict ordered thirty thousand shi of grain released for the market, and Bei Henuo and Vice President Tao Dai were charged with supervising the sale.
translations.idiomatic: The court released thirty thousand shi of grain for the market and put Bei Henuo and Vice President Tao Dai in charge of overseeing the trade.

sentences.zh: 事已，焞上表謝「八道生靈，賴以全活」。

translations.literal: When the affair was finished, Yi Sun submitted a memorial of thanks: "The people of the eight provinces owe their survival to this."
translations.idiomatic: When the relief effort was complete, Yi Sun sent a memorial of thanks stating that the people of Korea's eight provinces had been saved by it.

sentences.zh: 是年，授陝西巡撫。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed governor of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was appointed governor of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 疏報：「陝西開事例，積貯米麥，應存一百七十七萬石有奇，今實存僅十七萬。

translations.literal: In a memorial he reported: "Under Shaanxi's contribution-for-office system, stored rice and wheat should amount to more than 1.77 million shi; the actual stock is only 170,000."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that under Shaanxi's contribution-for-office system the province should have kept more than 1.77 million shi of rice and wheat in store, yet only 170,000 shi remained.

sentences.zh: 」上命尚書傅臘塔、張鵬翮往按。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered Ministers Fu Lata and Zhang Penghe to go and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Ministers Fu Lata and Zhang Penghe to investigate.

sentences.zh: 尋疏言長安、永壽、華陰等糴補三十八萬有奇，餘皆欠自捐生，請令補完。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he memorialized that Chang'an, Yongshou, Huayin, and other places had purchased grain to make up more than 380,000 shi; the remainder was owed by student donors, and he asked that they be ordered to make it good.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported that Chang'an, Yongshou, Huayin, and other counties had bought grain to restore more than 380,000 shi, and asked that the remaining shortfall owed by student donors be made up.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，調四川。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was transferred to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he was transferred to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「打箭爐、木鴉等處番、民一萬九千餘戶歸順，請增設安撫使五、副使五、土百戶四十五，以專管轄。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "At Dartsedo, Muya, and other places more than nineteen thousand barbarian and civilian households have submitted; I request that five pacification commissioners, five vice commissioners, and forty-five native company chiefs be added to govern them exclusively."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that more than nineteen thousand tribal and civilian households around Dartsedo and Muya who had submitted be placed under five new pacification commissioners, five vice commissioners, and forty-five native company chiefs.

sentences.zh: 邊民運茶赴爐貿易，給官引五千六百道，定額徵課。

translations.literal: Border people transport tea to the trading posts; 5,600 official permits should be issued and a fixed quota of tax levied.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed issuing 5,600 official permits for border people who haul tea to the trading posts and collecting tax at a fixed rate.

sentences.zh: 川省行鹽，潼川、中江山路崎嶇，難於陸運，額運壅滯。

translations.literal: In Sichuan salt is distributed overland; the mountain roads of Tongchuan and Zhongjiang are rugged, land transport is difficult, and the allotted shipments pile up.
translations.idiomatic: Because salt in Sichuan was moved overland, the rugged routes through Tongchuan and Zhongjiang made transport difficult and shipments backed up.

sentences.zh: 惟冰江小溪通水運，請增給水引，商民交便。

translations.literal: Only the Bingjiang Creek allows water transport; I request that additional water permits be granted so merchants and people may trade more conveniently.
translations.idiomatic: Only Bingjiang Creek could carry salt by water, so he asked for additional water-transport permits to make trade easier for merchants and the public.

sentences.zh: 」貝和諾治事精詳，尚書張鵬翮按事還，於上前亟稱之。

translations.literal: " Bei Henuo handled affairs with meticulous thoroughness; when Minister Zhang Penghe returned from his investigation, he repeatedly praised him before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Bei Henuo was meticulous in administration, and when Minister Zhang Penghe returned from his inspection he repeatedly praised him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，召授兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he was summoned and appointed vice president of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year he was recalled to the capital and appointed vice president of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，擢雲貴總督，捕治富民盜李天極、王枝葉等。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou and captured and punished the bandits of Fumin, Li Tianji, Wang Zhiye, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year he was made governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou and captured the Fumin bandits Li Tianji, Wang Zhiye, and their followers.

sentences.zh: 天極廣通諸生，與臨安硃六非造為符讖，師宗州枝葉，人素無行，天極等誘之，詭託明桂王孫，糾黨謀不軌。

translations.literal: Tianji was a licentiate of Guangtong; with Lin'an's Zhu Liufei he fabricated talismans and prophecies. Zhiye of Shizong Prefecture had always been a man of bad conduct; Tianji and the others enticed him, falsely claiming to act for a grandson of the Ming Prince of Gui, and gathered a faction to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tianji, a licentiate from Guangtong, joined Zhu Liufei of Lin'an in forging prophetic talismans. Wang Zhiye of Shizong, a man of ill repute, was drawn in by Tianji's group, who falsely claimed to represent a grandson of the Ming Prince of Gui and organized a conspiracy against the throne.

sentences.zh: 僭稱文興三年，散播印劄，圖劫掠廣南、開化，自蒙自竄入會城。

translations.literal: They presumptuously declared the third year of Wenxing, circulated printed proclamations, plotted to plunder Guangnan and Kaihua, and fled from Mengzi into the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: They proclaimed the third year of the fictitious Wenxing reign, distributed printed proclamations, planned raids on Guangnan and Kaihua, and fled from Mengzi toward the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 貝和諾標兵诇得狀，誅六人，流其餘黨。

translations.literal: Bei Henuo sent scouts and learned the situation; six men were executed and the rest of the faction were banished.
translations.idiomatic: Bei Henuo sent scouts to uncover the plot, executed six ringleaders, and banished the remaining conspirators.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，召拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he was summoned and appointed minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year he was recalled and appointed minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 以太原流匪陳四等六十餘人詭稱赴雲南墾地，貝和諾得布政使牒報不察究，坐降調，授盛京工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Because more than sixty fugitives from Taiyuan, Chen Si and others, had falsely claimed they were going to Yunnan to open wasteland and Bei Henuo, on receiving a report from the provincial treasurer, failed to investigate, he was demoted and transferred, and appointed vice president of the Ministry of Works at Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: When more than sixty Taiyuan fugitives led by Chen Si falsely claimed they were going to Yunnan to reclaim land, Bei Henuo failed to investigate a report from the provincial treasurer; he was demoted and reassigned as vice president of the Ministry of Works at Mukden.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，復召為禮部尚書，以老乞休，詔慰留。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he was again summoned as minister of Rites; on grounds of old age he requested retirement, and an edict comforted him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year he was again made minister of Rites; when he asked to retire because of age, the emperor issued an edict urging him to stay.

sentences.zh: 六十年，卒官。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the sixtieth year.

sentences.zh: 子馬喇，襲管佐領，兼護軍參領，累擢正紅旗滿洲副都統。

translations.literal: His son Mala inherited management of a company captaincy, concurrently served as a brigade adjutant, and was repeatedly promoted to Manchu vice commander of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mala inherited a company captaincy, also served as a brigade adjutant, and rose to become Manchu vice commander of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，西藏阿爾布巴等與貝子康濟鼐不睦，命馬喇往駐西藏。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, Arubaba and others in Tibet were at odds with Prince Kangjin Nai; Mala was ordered to go and be stationed in Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, after Arubaba and others in Tibet fell out with Prince Kangjin Nai, Mala was sent to take up residence in Tibet.

sentences.zh: 既，阿爾布巴戕害康濟鼐，後藏頗羅鼐率兵報仇，執阿爾布巴等。

translations.literal: Afterward Arubaba murdered Kangjin Nai; Poluo Zang of Rear Tibet led troops to avenge him and seized Arubaba and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Arubaba killed Kangjin Nai; Poluo Zang of Rear Tibet raised troops to avenge him and captured Arubaba and his associates.

sentences.zh: 遣尚書查郎阿等讞其罪，磔之。

translations.literal: Minister Zhala'a and others were dispatched to try their crimes; they were dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Minister Zhala'a and others to judge the case, and the culprits were executed by dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 詔頗羅鼐總管前後藏事，移達賴喇嘛於里塘。

translations.literal: An edict put Poluo Zang in overall charge of affairs in Front and Rear Tibet and moved the Dalai Lama to Litang.
translations.idiomatic: Poluo Zang was put in charge of both Front and Rear Tibet, and the Dalai Lama was moved to Litang.

sentences.zh: 七年，命馬喇駐里塘守護，賜帑金二千，總藏事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Mala was ordered to be stationed at Litang as guardian; he was granted two thousand taels from the treasury and put in overall charge of Tibetan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Mala was posted to Litang as guardian, given two thousand taels from the treasury, and placed in overall charge of Tibetan affairs.

sentences.zh: 擢護軍統領。

translations.literal: He was promoted to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 還京，遷工部尚書，坐免。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he was transferred to minister of Works, then dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital he was made minister of Works but was later dismissed for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 十一年，復以副都統銜往西藏辦事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was again sent to Tibet on business with the rank of vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was again dispatched to Tibet with the rank of vice commander.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving there.

sentences.zh: 陶岱，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正藍旗人。

translations.literal: Tao Dai, of the Guwalgiya clan, a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Dai was a Manchu of the Guwalgiya clan in the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 由主事歷戶部郎中，累擢吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: From secretary he served as department director in the Ministry of Revenue and was repeatedly promoted to vice president of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from secretary to department director in the Ministry of Revenue and was eventually promoted to vice president of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮告飢，乞開市貿穀，命陶岱與貝和諾運米給糴，御製海運朝鮮記紀其事。

translations.literal: Korea reported famine and begged to open a market to trade for grain; Tao Dai and Bei Henuo were ordered to transport rice for sale, and the emperor's own composition "Record of Sea Transport to Korea" commemorated the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Korea reported famine and asked to open a market for grain, Tao Dai and Bei Henuo were ordered to ship rice for sale; the emperor commemorated the episode in his "Record of Sea Transport to Korea."

sentences.zh: 康熙三十八年，署兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi he served as acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi he served as acting governor-general of Jiangnan and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 尋授倉場侍郎，以漕運遲誤，降五秩，隨旗行走。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed vice president of the Granary Administration; because grain transport was delayed he was demoted five ranks and assigned to serve with his banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice president of the Granary Administration, but after grain transport fell behind schedule he was demoted five ranks and reduced to banner service.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 博霽，巴雅拉氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Bo Ji, of the Bayara clan, a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Ji was a Manchu of the Bayara clan in the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 自護衛授鑾儀使，擢鑲白旗都統。

translations.literal: From imperial guard he was appointed director of ceremonial guards and promoted to commander of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the imperial guard to director of ceremonial guards and then to commander of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十四年，授江寧將軍，調西安。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi he was appointed general of Jiangning and transferred to Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi he was made general of Jiangning and then transferred to Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，撫遠大將軍費揚古率師西剿噶爾丹，命博霽率滿洲兵自寧夏會師，大敗噶爾丹於昭莫多。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year Grand General Fei Yanggu led an army west to suppress Galdan; Bo Ji was ordered to lead Manchu troops from Ningxia to join the force and Galdan was heavily defeated at Jao Modo.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year Grand General Fei Yanggu marched west against Galdan; Bo Ji led Manchu troops from Ningxia to join him, and Galdan was routed at Jao Modo.

sentences.zh: 敘功，授世職拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded and he was granted the hereditary rank of Tashala Han.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was granted the hereditary rank of Tashala Han.

sentences.zh: 聖祖嘗諭大學士等曰：「博霽自江寧赴西安，軍民攀留泣送，直至浦口。

translations.literal: The Kangxi Emperor once instructed the grand secretaries and others: "When Bo Ji went from Jiangning to Xi'an, soldiers and civilians clung to him weeping as they saw him off, all the way to Pukou."
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor once told the grand secretaries: "When Bo Ji left Jiangning for Xi'an, soldiers and civilians wept and begged him to stay, escorting him in tears as far as Pukou."

sentences.zh: 非有善政，何能如此？

translations.literal: Without good governance, how could this be so?
translations.idiomatic: Without good governance, how could he have won such devotion?

sentences.zh: 誠可謂將軍矣！

translations.literal: He may truly be called a general!
translations.idiomatic: Truly he deserves to be called a general!

sentences.zh: 」四十二年，上幸西安閱兵，諭曰：「西安官兵皆嫺禮節，重和睦，尚廉恥，且人才壯健，騎射精練。

translations.literal: " In the forty-second year the emperor visited Xi'an to review the troops and instructed: "The officers and soldiers of Xi'an are all well versed in etiquette, value harmony, esteem integrity and shame, and moreover their men are strong and their horsemanship and archery finely practiced."
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year, during an imperial inspection of troops at Xi'an, the emperor declared: "Xi'an's officers and soldiers are courteous, value harmony and honor, and are strong, skilled riders and archers."

sentences.zh: 朕巡幸江南、浙江、盛京、烏喇等處閱兵，末有能及之者，深可嘉尚！

translations.literal: When I toured Jiangnan, Zhejiang, Mukden, Wula, and other places to review troops, none could match them; this is deeply praiseworthy!
translations.idiomatic: In all my troop reviews in Jiangnan, Zhejiang, Mukden, Wula, and elsewhere, I have seen none to equal them—highly commendable!

sentences.zh: 」賚博霽御用櫜建、弓矢。

translations.literal: " Bo Ji was granted the emperor's own quiver and bow and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then bestowed on Bo Ji his own quiver, bow, and arrows.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，授四川陝西總督。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was appointed governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he was appointed governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 上以山、陝屢歲祲，欲於河南儲粟備賑，溯黃河挽運，慮三門砥柱水急，舟不得上，命博霽偕山、陝、河南巡撫會勘。

translations.literal: Because Shaanxi and Shanxi had suffered repeated bad harvests, the emperor wished to store grain in Henan for relief; hauling it up the Yellow River, he feared the swift water at Sanmen and the Pillars of the River would prevent boats from ascending, and ordered Bo Ji together with the governors of Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Henan to inspect jointly.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated famine in Shaanxi and Shanxi, the emperor wanted to store grain in Henan for relief and haul it up the Yellow River, but worried that the rapids at Sanmen Gorge would block boats; he ordered Bo Ji and the governors of Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Henan to survey the route together.

sentences.zh: 尋合疏言：「三門灘多水激，挽運險阻，仍以陸運為便。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they jointly memorialized: "At Sanmen the shoals have much churning water; hauling grain there is dangerous and difficult, and land transport is still more convenient."
translations.idiomatic: They soon jointly reported that the churning waters at Sanmen Gorge made upstream hauling too dangerous and that overland transport remained the better option.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted their recommendation.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he died; the court granted sacrificial rites and funeral honors.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-seventh year, and the court bestowed state funeral rites upon him.

sentences.zh: 覺羅華顯，滿洲正紅旗人。

translations.literal: Aisin Gioro Hua Xian, a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xian, a Manchu of the Aisin Gioro clan in the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 初授宗人府主事，遷戶部理事官。

translations.literal: He was first appointed a secretary in the Imperial Clan Court and transferred to an administrative officer in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a secretary in the Imperial Clan Court and then as an administrative officer in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十七年，授翰林院侍講學士，累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year of Kangxi he was appointed a Hanlin reader-in-waiting and was repeatedly promoted to a grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year of Kangxi he became a Hanlin reader-in-waiting and eventually rose to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，授甘肅巡撫，未上官，調陝西。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was appointed governor of Gansu; before taking office he was transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he was appointed governor of Gansu but was transferred to Shaanxi before assuming that post.

sentences.zh: 四十年，擢川陝總督。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 甘肅流民數千人就賑西安，華顯與巡撫鄂海出俸為有司倡，集資計口授糧，並撥荒地為業。

translations.literal: Several thousand refugees from Gansu came to Xi'an seeking relief; Hua Xian and Governor E Hai contributed their salaries to set an example for local officials, collected funds and distributed grain by head count, and also allocated wasteland for livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: When several thousand Gansu refugees sought relief in Xi'an, Hua Xian and Governor E Hai donated their salaries to set an example, raised funds to distribute grain by head count, and assigned wasteland for them to farm.

sentences.zh: 上幸西安閱兵，與博霽、鄂海同受賜。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Xi'an to review the troops, he and Bo Ji and E Hai all received gifts together.
translations.idiomatic: During the emperor's troop review at Xi'an, he received imperial gifts along with Bo Ji and E Hai.

sentences.zh: 陝民困重斂，華顯飭有司禁私徵，屏絕餽遺，軍民稱頌。

translations.literal: The people of Shaanxi were burdened by heavy levies; Hua Xian ordered officials to forbid unauthorized collections, shut out gifts entirely, and soldiers and civilians praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Because the people of Shaanxi were crushed by heavy levies, Hua Xian forbade unauthorized collections and refused all gifts; both soldiers and civilians praised him.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，卒官，加太子太保，贈兵部尚書，諡文襄。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he died in office; he was posthumously given the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted the posthumous office of minister of War, and given the temple name Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the forty-second year and was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and minister of War, with the title Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 祀陝西名宦。

translations.literal: He was enshrined among the distinguished officials of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined in the hall of distinguished officials of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 蔣陳錫，字雨亭，江南常熟人。

translations.literal: Jiang Chenxi, styled Yuting, a native of Changshu in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Chenxi, styled Yuting, was a native of Changshu in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父伊，康熙十二年進士，選庶吉士，授御史。

translations.literal: His father Yi was a jinshi of the twelfth year of Kangxi, selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and appointed a censor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Kangxi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and served as a censor.

sentences.zh: 疏陳民間疾苦，繪十二圖以進。

translations.literal: In memorials he set forth the people's hardships and painted twelve pictures to present.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on the people's hardships and submitted twelve illustrative paintings.

sentences.zh: 累官河南提學道副使，卒官。

translations.literal: He rose to vice commissioner of the Henan education circuit and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually became vice commissioner of the Henan education circuit and died in office.

sentences.zh: 陳錫，康熙二十四年進士，授陝西富平知縣。

translations.literal: Chenxi was a jinshi of the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi and was appointed magistrate of Fuping in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Chenxi passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi and was appointed magistrate of Fuping in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，米斛直數千，發倉賑濟，不給，斥家資佐之，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: In a year of famine a hu of rice cost several thousand cash; he opened the granary for relief, and when that was insufficient he spent his family wealth to assist, saving very many lives.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine when a hu of rice cost thousands of cash, he opened the granary for relief and, when that was not enough, spent his own family's wealth as well, saving a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 行取，擢禮部主事。

translations.literal: Selected for capital service, he was promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for service in the capital, he was promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 監督海運倉，革糧艘篷席例銀。

translations.literal: Supervising the sea-transport granary, he abolished the customary silver payment for grain-boat awnings and matting.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising the sea-transport granary, he abolished the customary fee for grain-boat awnings and matting.

sentences.zh: 遷員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 河道總督張鵬翮薦佐兩淮河務。

translations.literal: Grand Canal governor Zhang Penghe recommended him to assist with the Two Huai river works.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Canal governor Zhang Penghe recommended him to assist with river works on the Huai.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，授直隸天津道，遷河南按察使，讞決平恕。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he was appointed intendant of Tianjin in Zhili and transferred to judicial commissioner of Henan; his judgments were fair and lenient.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year he became intendant of Tianjin in Zhili and then judicial commissioner of Henan, where his judgments were noted for fairness and moderation.

sentences.zh: 豫省有老瓜賊為害行旅，陳錫廉得其巢穴，悉擒治之。

translations.literal: In Henan the Laogua bandits harmed travelers; Chenxi through integrity learned their lair and captured and punished them all.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan the Laogua bandits preyed on travelers; through careful investigation Jiang Chenxi found their hideout and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，遷山東布政使。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he was transferred to treasurer of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he was made treasurer of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢任巡撫。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to governor.

sentences.zh: 疏請緩徵二十三​​州、縣、衛被災逋賦，廣鄉試解額，增給買補營馬直，免累及所司。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting deferred collection of overdue taxes from twenty-three prefectures, counties, and garrisons stricken by disaster, an expanded provincial quota for the civil examinations, increased allowances for purchasing replacement garrison horses, and exemption of responsible officials from liability.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that overdue taxes from twenty-three disaster-stricken prefectures, counties, and garrisons be deferred, that the provincial examination quota be expanded, that allowances for replacing garrison horses be increased, and that responsible officials not be punished for shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 條陳海防三事，言戰船當更番修葺，水手當召募熟諳水道之人，沿海村莊當舉行團練，互相接應；

translations.literal: He set forth three items on coastal defense: warships should be repaired in rotation; sailors should be recruited from men skilled and familiar with the waterways; coastal villages should organize militia training for mutual support;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed three coastal defense measures: warships should be repaired on a rotating schedule, sailors should be recruited from men who knew the local waters, and coastal villages should organize militia for mutual defense;

sentences.zh: 並以御史陳汝咸條議海疆弭盜，疏請漁舟編甲，閩、粵鳥船不許攜砲械，得盜舟火藥軍器，必究所從來。

translations.literal: and citing Censor Chen Ruqian's proposals for suppressing piracy on the maritime frontier, he memorialized requesting that fishing boats be registered by household, that Fujian and Guangdong "bird ships" be forbidden to carry cannon and weapons, and that whenever pirate boats, gunpowder, or military arms were seized, their source must be traced.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on Censor Chen Ruqian's proposals to suppress coastal piracy, he also asked that fishing boats be registered by household, that Fujian and Guangdong bird ships be barred from carrying arms, and that the source of any seized pirate vessels, gunpowder, or weapons be rigorously investigated.

sentences.zh: 部議悉從之。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry approved all of his proposals.

sentences.zh: 長蘆巡鹽御史希祿請增東省鹽引，臨清關請增設濟寧等五州縣口岸，陳錫皆言其不便，並得請。

translations.literal: Changlu salt censor Xilu requested an increase in Shandong salt permits; the Linqing customs post requested adding customs stations at Jining and four other prefectures and counties; Chenxi said in each case that it would be inconvenient, and in each case his objection was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Changlu salt censor Xilu proposed increasing Shandong salt permits and the Linqing customs office asked to add stations at Jining and four other prefectures and counties, Jiang Chenxi argued against both measures, and the court accepted his objections.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，擢雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year of Kangxi he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 祿勸州土酋常應運誘沿江土夷攻卓幹寨，陳錫檄師會剿，平之，撥兵弁駐守其地。

translations.literal: The native chieftain Chang Yingyun of Luquan Prefecture incited riverside tribal peoples to attack Zhuogan Stockade; Chenxi dispatched troops for joint suppression, pacified them, and assigned officers and soldiers to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: When Luquan chieftain Chang Yingyun incited riverside tribes to attack Zhuogan Stockade, Jiang Chenxi sent troops to join the suppression, restored order, and stationed officers and soldiers to hold the site.

sentences.zh: 石羊緒礦廠硐老山空，課額不足，疏請嗣後硐衰即止，勿制定額。

translations.literal: At the Shiyangxu mine the old tunnels had been exhausted and the quota assessment fell short; he memorialized requesting that in future collection cease when the mine declined, and that no fixed quota be set.
translations.idiomatic: When exhaustion of the Shiyangxu mine left it unable to meet its quota, he asked that future levies stop once a mine declined rather than enforcing a fixed assessment.

sentences.zh: 鎮遠至省三十二驛，山路崎嶇，驛夫苦累，下令非有符合，毋濫應夫馬。

translations.literal: From Zhenyuan to the provincial capital there were thirty-two courier stations; the mountain roads were rugged and the couriers suffered hardship; he ordered that unless there was a valid warrant, laborers and horses must not be supplied indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: The thirty-two courier stations between Zhenyuan and the provincial capital crossed rugged mountain roads that overburdened the couriers; he ruled that draft labor and horses must not be supplied without a proper warrant.

sentences.zh: 都統武格、將軍噶爾弼率師入西藏，以雲南糧運艱難，欲自四川運糧濟給。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Wuge and General Ga'erbi led an army into Tibet; because grain transport from Yunnan was difficult, they wished to supply troops from Sichuan grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Commander-in-Chief Wuge and General Ga'erbi marched into Tibet, they sought to supply the campaign from Sichuan because Yunnan grain transport was too difficult.

sentences.zh: 四川總督年羹堯奏言滇、蜀俱進兵，蜀糧不足兼供。

translations.literal: Sichuan governor-general Nian Gengyao memorialized that both Yunnan and Sichuan were advancing troops and Sichuan grain was insufficient to supply both.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan governor-general Nian Gengyao reported that with both Yunnan and Sichuan committing troops, Sichuan's grain reserves could not supply both fronts.

sentences.zh: 乃命陳錫與巡撫甘國璧速運。

translations.literal: The court then ordered Chenxi and Surveillance Commissioner Gan Guobi to transport grain speedily.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Jiang Chenxi and Yunnan governor Gan Guobi to rush grain shipments immediately.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，詔責其籌濟不力誤軍機，與國璧並奪職，令自備資斧運米入藏。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year an edict rebuked them for failing to supply provisions effectively and thus botching military affairs; Chenxi and Guobi were both stripped of office and ordered to supply their own funds and tools to transport rice into Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year an edict blamed them for bungling grain supply and disrupting the campaign; both Jiang Chenxi and Gan Guobi were dismissed and ordered to transport rice into Tibet at their own expense.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒於途。

translations.literal: The next year he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died en route.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，山東巡撫黃炳言陳錫在巡撫任，侵蝕捐穀羨餘銀二百餘萬，部議督追。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, Shandong governor Huang Bing reported that during Chenxi's term as governor he had embezzled more than two million taels of surplus silver from donated grain; the ministry recommended supervising recovery.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 Shandong governor Huang Bing reported that Jiang Chenxi had embezzled over two million taels in surplus funds from donated grain while serving as governor; the ministry ordered supervised recovery.

sentences.zh: 弟廷錫入陳始末，詔減償其半。

translations.literal: His younger brother Tingsi presented the full account; an edict reduced the restitution by half.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Tingsi petitioned with the full story, and the court halved the required restitution.

sentences.zh: 子漣、泂。

translations.literal: His sons were Lian and Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Lian and Jiong.

sentences.zh: 漣，字檀人。

translations.literal: Lian, styled Tanren.
translations.idiomatic: Lian, styled Tanren.

sentences.zh: 進士，官編修，終太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: A jinshi, he served as compiler in the Hanlin Academy and ended as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi, he rose to compiler in the Hanlin Academy and ended his career as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 泂，字愷思。

translations.literal: Jiong, styled Kaisi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong, styled Kaisi.

sentences.zh: 進士，歷工部郎中，出為雲南提學道。

translations.literal: A jinshi, he successively served as director in the Ministry of Works and was then appointed educational intendant of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi, he served as a director in the Ministry of Works before becoming Yunnan's educational intendant.

sentences.zh: 西陲用兵，命從軍，授甘肅涼莊道。

translations.literal: When war broke out on the western frontier he was ordered to join the campaign and was appointed circuit intendant of Liangzhuang in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: When war erupted on the western frontier he was ordered to the front and appointed circuit intendant of Liangzhuang in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 西檄多卜藏、瑪嘉諸部與謝勒蘇、額勒布兩部逃人倚石門寺為巢，往來劫掠。

translations.literal: In the western regions tribes such as Duobuzang and Majia, together with fugitives from the Xielesu and Elebu tribes, made Shimen Temple their base and raided back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: In western Gansu, tribes including Duobuzang and Majia and fugitives from the Xielesu and Elebu groups used Shimen Temple as a base for raiding.

sentences.zh: 泂料簡精銳，會涼州鎮官兵，分五路進剿，轉戰棋子山，殲賊之半。

translations.literal: Jiong selected elite troops, joined with the garrison forces of Liangzhou, advanced in five columns to suppress them, fought around Qizi Mountain, and destroyed half the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong picked elite troops, combined with Liangzhou garrison forces, attacked in five columns through Qizi Mountain, and destroyed half the raiders.

sentences.zh: 時羅卜藏丹津進逼西寧，复檄兵捍禦，羅卜藏丹津遁走。

translations.literal: At that time Lobzang Danjin was pressing toward Xining; Jiong again mustered troops to resist, and Lobzang Danjin fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Lobzang Danjin threatened Xining, Jiong rallied troops to block him and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 大將軍年羹堯上其功，遷山西按察使，進布政使。

translations.literal: Grand General Nian Gengyao reported his merit; he was transferred to Shanxi provincial surveillance commissioner and promoted to provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Nian Gengyao commended his service; he was made Shanxi surveillance commissioner and then promoted to provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上嘉泂實心供職，免其父追償。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Jiong for serving with genuine devotion and remitted his father's restitution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Jiong's conscientious service and waived his father's restitution debt.

sentences.zh: 雍正十年，加侍郎銜，往肅州經理軍營屯田。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongzheng he was given the honorary rank of vice president and sent to Suzhou to manage military garrison land reclamation.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 10 he received the honorary rank of vice president and was sent to Suzhou to oversee military land reclamation.

sentences.zh: 在事二年，闢鎮番柳林湖田十三萬畝，得糧三萬石。

translations.literal: In two years of service he opened 130,000 mu of fields at Zhenfan's Liulin Lake and obtained 30,000 shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In two years he reclaimed 130,000 mu around Liulin Lake at Zhenfan and harvested 30,000 shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 築河堤，擴二大渠，分濬支渠，並建倉儲糧，公私饒裕。

translations.literal: He built river dikes, expanded two major canals, dredged branch channels, and erected granaries to store grain, so that public and private interests alike flourished.
translations.idiomatic: He built dikes, expanded two main canals, dredged branch channels, and built granaries until both the state and local people prospered.

sentences.zh: 副都御史二格協理軍需，劾泂侵帑誤公，逮治論死，下獄追贓。

translations.literal: Vice censor-in-chief Erge, assisting in military supplies, impeached Jiong for embezzling public funds and neglecting duty; he was arrested, sentenced to death, imprisoned, and forced to repay stolen goods.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Erge, handling military supplies, accused Jiong of embezzlement and neglect; Jiong was arrested, sentenced to death, imprisoned, and ordered to repay stolen funds.

sentences.zh: 總督查郎阿等交章雪其誣，泂已病卒。

translations.literal: Governor-general Cha Lang'a and others submitted successive memorials clearing him of false charges, but Jiong had already died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Cha Lang'a and others filed memorial after memorial to clear his name, but Jiong had already died of illness.

sentences.zh: 劉廕樞，字喬南，陝西韓城人。

translations.literal: Liu Yinshu, styled Qiaonan, a native of Hancheng in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yinshu, styled Qiaonan, was a native of Hancheng in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙十五年進士，授河南蘭陽知縣，有政聲。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fifteenth year of Kangxi, he was appointed magistrate of Lanyang in Henan and won a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Kangxi 15, he became magistrate of Lanyang in Henan and earned a reputation for sound administration.

sentences.zh: 行取，擢吏科給事中，以憂歸，服闋，除刑科給事中。

translations.literal: Selected for capital service, he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Personnel Section; he returned home on mourning leave, and after the mourning period ended was appointed supervising secretary in the Punishments Section.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for the capital, he became a supervising secretary in the Personnel Section; after mourning leave he returned as a supervising secretary in the Punishments Section.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「廉吏必節儉。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "An upright official must be frugal.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "An upright official must live frugally.

sentences.zh: 邇來居官競尚侈靡，不特車馬、衣服、飲食、器用，僭制逾等；

translations.literal: Recently officials in office compete in extravagance; not only in carriages, horses, clothing, food, and utensils do they exceed their rank and transgress regulations;
translations.idiomatic: Officials now compete in extravagance—not only exceeding rank in carriages, horses, dress, food, and furnishings,

sentences.zh: 抑且交結、奔走、餽送、夤緣，棄如泥沙，用如流水。

translations.literal: they also in forming connections, running about, giving gifts, and currying favor throw money away like mud and sand and spend it like flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: but also on networking, courting favor, and gift-giving they squander money like dirt and spend it like water.

sentences.zh: 俸不給則貸於人，玷官箴，傷國體。

translations.literal: When salaries do not suffice they borrow from others, staining official integrity and harming the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: When salaries fall short they borrow, staining official honor and damaging the state's dignity.

sentences.zh: 請敕申斥，以厲廉戒貪。

translations.literal: He requested an imperial command of stern rebuke to encourage integrity and warn against greed.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the throne to issue stern rebukes to promote integrity and deter corruption.

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「京師放債，六七當十；

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "In the capital money is lent at six or seven for ten;
translations.idiomatic: " He also reported: "In the capital, lenders charge six or seven cash for every ten lent;

sentences.zh: 半年不償，即行轉票，以子為母。

translations.literal: if not repaid within half a year the debt is converted to a promissory note, with interest becoming principal.
translations.idiomatic: unpaid debts after six months roll over, with interest added to principal.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，累萬盈千。

translations.literal: Within a few years debts mount to tens of thousands and thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In a few years debts mount to thousands and tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 是朝廷職官，竟為債主廝養。

translations.literal: Thus court officials end up kept like servants by their creditors.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials thus become beholden to moneylenders like domestic servants.

sentences.zh: 乞敕嚴立科條，照實貸銀數三分起息。

translations.literal: He begged that strict regulations be established, with interest fixed at three percent on the actual amount lent.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that strict rules cap interest at three percent of the principal actually lent.

sentences.zh: 」並下部議行。

translations.literal: " Both memorials were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " Both proposals were sent to the ministries for deliberation and adoption.

sentences.zh: 尋調戶科。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，詔求直言，廕樞疏請肅紀綱，覈名實，開言路，報可。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year the throne solicited frank counsel; Yinshu memorialized requesting restoration of discipline, verification of names and realities, and opening of channels for remonstrance; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year, when the throne solicited frank criticism, Yinshu asked for restored discipline, verified appointments, and open channels of remonstrance; the court assented.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，外轉江西贛南道。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was transferred outside the capital to the Gannan Circuit in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he was posted to the Gannan Circuit in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 贛俗健訟，廕樞晝夜平決，懲妄訴者，訟漸稀。

translations.literal: The people of Ganzhou were fond of litigation; Yinshu adjudicated day and night, punished frivolous plaintiffs, and lawsuits gradually grew rare.
translations.idiomatic: Ganzhou was notoriously litigious; Yinshu heard cases day and night, punished false suits, and litigation gradually declined.

sentences.zh: 將吏私徵門稅，廕樞令革之。

translations.literal: Military officers and clerks were privately collecting gate taxes; Yinshu ordered the practice abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When officers and clerks illegally collected gate taxes, Yinshu abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 米市有牙課，牙人籍以婪索。

translations.literal: The rice market had broker fees, and brokers used them as license for extortion.
translations.idiomatic: Broker fees in the rice market gave brokers license to extort.

sentences.zh: 廕樞以其錢置田，徵租代課，除民累。

translations.literal: Yinshu used the money to buy land, collected rent in lieu of the fees, and removed the people's burden.
translations.idiomatic: Yinshu used the fees to buy land whose rent replaced the levy, relieving the people's burden.

sentences.zh: 署按察使，忤總督阿山，以讞獄前後獄辭互異，劾罷。
