translations.literal: Acting as provincial surveillance commissioner, he offended Governor-general Ashan, who impeached and dismissed him on the grounds that the testimony in a criminal case was inconsistent before and after adjudication.
translations.idiomatic: While acting surveillance commissioner he clashed with Governor-general Ashan, who impeached and dismissed him over inconsistent testimony in a criminal case.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，聖祖西巡，廕樞迎駕潼關，上識之，召對稱旨，复授雲南按察使。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year the Sacred Ancestor toured the west; Yinshu welcomed the imperial progress at Tong Pass; the emperor recognized him, summoned him for audience and found his answers pleasing, and again appointed him Yunnan provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year, when Kangxi toured the west, Yinshu welcomed him at Tong Pass; the emperor recognized him, was pleased by their audience, and reappointed him Yunnan surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，遷廣東布政使。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was transferred to Guangdong provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he became Guangdong provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 總督貝和諾稱其清廉勤慎，士民愛戴，雲南布政使缺員，請以廕樞調補，上從之。

translations.literal: Governor-general Bei Henuo praised his integrity, diligence, and prudence and the affection of officials and people; when the Yunnan provincial administration commissioner post fell vacant he requested Yinshu be transferred to fill it, and the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Bei Henuo praised his integrity and diligence and the people's affection for him; when Yunnan's administration commissioner post opened, he recommended Yinshu for transfer, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 廕樞督濬昆明湖，築六河岸徬。

translations.literal: Yinshu supervised dredging of Kunming Lake and built embankments along the six rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Yinshu oversaw dredging of Kunming Lake and built embankments along six rivers.

sentences.zh: 會夏旱，發粟平糶，禱於五華山，得雨，民大悅。

translations.literal: When summer drought occurred he released grain for sale at fair prices, prayed on Wuhua Mountain, rain fell, and the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: During a summer drought he sold grain at fair prices, prayed on Wuhua Mountain, rain came, and the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，擢貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he was promoted to governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he was promoted to governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 貴州苗、仲雜處，號難治。

translations.literal: In Guizhou Miao and Zhong peoples lived intermixed and it was called difficult to govern.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou, where Miao and Zhong peoples lived intermixed, was regarded as hard to govern.

sentences.zh: 廕樞至，絕餽遺，省徭役，務以安靜為治。

translations.literal: When Yinshu arrived he rejected gifts, reduced corvée labor, and made quiet governance his aim.
translations.idiomatic: On arriving Yinshu refused gifts, reduced corvée burdens, and governed through quiet restraint.

sentences.zh: 疏請廣鄉試解額，設南籠廳學，以振人文。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting an expanded provincial examination quota and the establishment of a Nanlong subprefecture school to revive local culture.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for an expanded provincial examination quota and a Nanlong subprefecture school to revive local culture.

sentences.zh: 先後請改石阡、丹川、西堡、寧谷、平州、大華諸土司，設流官。

translations.literal: He successively requested converting the native chieftaincies of Shiqian, Danchuan, Xibao, Ningu, Pingzhou, Dahua, and others to direct administration by appointed officials.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly petitioned to replace the native chieftaincies of Shiqian, Danchuan, Xibao, Ningu, Pingzhou, Dahua, and others with appointed officials.

sentences.zh: 開驛道，自雲南坡至蕉溪二千餘裡。

translations.literal: He opened a courier route more than two thousand li from Yunnan Slope to Jiaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: He opened a courier route of more than two thousand li from Yunnan Slope to Jiaoxi.

sentences.zh: 又疏言貴州錢糧課稅僅十餘萬，鄰省歲協餉二十餘萬，稍愆期，軍士懸額待餉。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that Guizhou's grain taxes and levies totaled only a little over 100,000 taels, while neighboring provinces annually contributed over 200,000 taels in aid; when payment was slightly late soldiers went hungry waiting for rations.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that Guizhou raised only about 100,000 taels in taxes while relying on over 200,000 taels in yearly aid from neighboring provinces; any delay left soldiers hungry waiting for pay.

sentences.zh: 請豫撥二十萬儲布政使庫。

translations.literal: He requested that 200,000 taels be allocated in advance and stored in the provincial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that 200,000 taels be allocated in advance to the provincial treasury.

sentences.zh: 部議持不可，疏三上，詔特允之。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and held that it was impermissible; after three memorials the throne specially approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry objected, but after three memorials the throne made an exception and approved.

sentences.zh: 其後紅苗叛，餉賴以無絀。

translations.literal: Later when the Red Miao rebelled, pay was sustained without shortage thanks to this reserve.
translations.idiomatic: When the Red Miao later rebelled, the reserve kept supplies from running short.

sentences.zh: 烏蒙、威寧兩土司相仇殺，四川巡撫年羹堯遣吏勘問，土酋匿不出，疏聞，命四川、雲、貴督撫按治。

translations.literal: The native chieftaincies of Wumeng and Weining feuded and killed one another; Sichuan governor Nian Gengyao sent officials to investigate, but the chieftains hid and would not appear; when this was reported the court ordered the governors of Sichuan, Yunnan, and Guizhou to investigate and settle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wumeng and Weining chieftaincies feuded, Sichuan governor Nian Gengyao sent investigators, but the chieftains refused to appear; the court then ordered the governors of Sichuan, Yunnan, and Guizhou to settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 廕樞先至，遣使招諭，威寧土酋聽命，烏蒙土酋亦自縛出就質，咸原伏罪釋仇，苗以無事。

translations.literal: Yinshu arrived first, sent envoys to summon and instruct them; the Weining chieftain obeyed, and the Wumeng chieftain also bound himself and came forth to stand trial; all willingly submitted, confessed guilt, and released their enmity, and the Miao districts were untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: Yinshu arrived first, sent envoys to summon them; the Weining chieftain complied, and the Wumeng chieftain bound himself and came to trial; all submitted, made peace, and the Miao districts were untroubled.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，準噶爾策妄阿喇布坦侵哈密，詔備兵進討。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year the Dzungar Tsewang Arabtan invaded Hami and an edict ordered troops prepared for a punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year Tsewang Arabtan of Dzungaria invaded Hami, and the court ordered troops mobilized for a punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 廕樞累疏請緩師，略云：「小丑不足煩大兵。

translations.literal: Yinshu repeatedly memorialized requesting delay of the campaign, saying in brief: "A petty foe is not worth troubling a great army.
translations.idiomatic: Yinshu repeatedly asked to delay the campaign, writing in part: "A petty foe does not warrant a major mobilization.

sentences.zh: 原皇上息怒，重內治，輕遠略。

translations.literal: I pray that Your Majesty may lay aside anger, emphasize internal governance, and give lesser weight to distant expansion."
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will set aside anger, focus on internal governance, and not overreach on distant frontiers."

sentences.zh: 」上責其妄奏，命馳驛赴軍前週閱詳議。

translations.literal: " The emperor rebuked him for presumptuous memorializing and ordered him to proceed by courier post to the front for detailed inspection and deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor rebuked him for presumption and ordered him to the front by express courier for a full review.

sentences.zh: 廕樞抵巴里坤，上疏數千言，請屯兵哈密，以逸待勞。

translations.literal: Yinshu reached Barkol and submitted a memorial of several thousand characters requesting that troops be stationed at Hami to await the enemy at ease while he grew weary.
translations.idiomatic: At Barkol Yinshu submitted a long memorial urging that troops hold Hami and wait out the enemy at ease.

sentences.zh: 旋稱病還甘肅，疏乞休，嚴旨譙讓，仍令回巡撫任。

translations.literal: He soon claimed illness and returned to Gansu, memorialized requesting retirement; a stern edict reproached him, yet he was still ordered back to his governor's post.
translations.idiomatic: He soon claimed illness and returned to Gansu to request retirement; though sharply rebuked, he was ordered back to his governorship.

sentences.zh: 廕樞疏報病癒，上斥廕樞：「令詣軍前即稱病，令回任病頓愈，情偽顯然。

translations.literal: Yinshu memorialized reporting recovery from illness; the emperor rebuked Yinshu: "Ordered to the front you at once fell ill; ordered back to office your illness suddenly healed—the deceit is obvious.
translations.idiomatic: When Yinshu reported his recovery, the emperor rebuked him: "Ordered to the front you fell ill; ordered back to office you suddenly recovered—the deceit is obvious.

sentences.zh: 」命解任詣京師。

translations.literal: " He was ordered stripped of office and to proceed to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " He was dismissed and ordered to the capital.

sentences.zh: 部議阻撓軍務，坐絞，上宥之，遣赴喀爾喀種地。

translations.literal: The ministry recommended the charge of obstructing military affairs, with the penalty of strangulation; the emperor pardoned him and sent him to farm in Khalkha.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry recommended strangulation for obstructing military affairs; the emperor pardoned him and sent him to farm in Khalkha.

sentences.zh: 年已八十二，居戍三年，釋還，復故官。

translations.literal: He was already eighty-two; after three years in exile he was released and restored to his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Already eighty-two, after three years of exile he was released and restored to rank.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，與千叟宴。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year he attended the banquet for a thousand elders.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year he attended the banquet for a thousand elders.

sentences.zh: 世宗御極，召見，賜金歸里。

translations.literal: When the Shizong ascended the throne Yinshu was summoned for audience, granted gold, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongzheng ascended the throne Yinshu was summoned, granted gold, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年八十七。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died, aged eighty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, aged eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 音泰，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Yin Tai, of the Guwalgiya clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Tai of the Guwalgiya clan was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 初為西安駐防兵。

translations.literal: At first he was a garrison soldier stationed at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a garrison soldier at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，副都統佛尼勒討吳三桂將譚弘、吳之茂、王屏籓等，音泰隸麾下。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi Lieutenant-general Foni'e campaigned against Wu Sangui's generals Tan Hong, Wu Zhimao, Wang Pingfan, and others; Yin Tai served under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 Lieutenant-general Foni'e fought Wu Sangui's generals Tan Hong, Wu Zhimao, and Wang Pingfan; Yin Tai served under him.

sentences.zh: 師自漢中進克陽平朝天關，駐守梅嶺關，賊夜劫營，音泰力禦，中槍折齒，得上賞。

translations.literal: The army advanced from Hanzhong and captured Yangping Chaotian Pass, garrisoned Meiling Pass; the rebels raided the camp by night; Yin Tai fought hard in defense, was shot and broke a tooth, and received a high reward.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced from Hanzhong, took Yangping Chaotian Pass, and garrisoned Meiling Pass; when rebels raided the camp at night Yin Tai fought them off, was shot and broke a tooth, and received a high reward.

sentences.zh: 明年，佛尼埒攻王輔臣秦州，臨壕列圍，賊突騎出犯，音泰射殪三人，賊駭遁。

translations.literal: The next year Foni'e attacked Wang Fuchen at Qinzhou, drew up siege lines by the moat; rebel cavalry charged out; Yin Tai shot and killed three men and the rebels fled in terror.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Foni'e besieged Wang Fuchen at Qinzhou; when rebel cavalry charged out Yin Tai killed three with his bow and the enemy fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 復進攻西和，屢敗之茂等於鹽關岐山堡。

translations.literal: Advancing again against Xihe he repeatedly defeated Zhimao and others at Yan Pass and Qishan Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Xihe he repeatedly defeated Zhimao and others at Yan Pass and Qishan Fort.

sentences.zh: 十七年，進攻四川，克保寧、敘州。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he advanced into Sichuan and captured Baoning and Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he entered Sichuan and captured Baoning and Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 敘功，授驍騎校，遷防禦。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed he was appointed daring cavalry commandant and transferred to garrison captain.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made daring cavalry commandant and then garrison captain.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，署參領，從西安將軍博霽會大將軍費揚古徵噶爾丹，出西路。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, acting as company commander, he followed Xi'an General Bo Ji to join Grand General Fei Yanggu in campaigning against Galdan by the western route.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year, acting company commander, he joined Xi'an General Bo Ji and Grand General Fei Yanggu's western campaign against Galdan.

sentences.zh: 五月，上親征，出中路，至克魯倫河。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the emperor personally campaigned, taking the central route to the Kerulen River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor took the field on the central route to the Kerulen River.

sentences.zh: 值積雨，運糧滯，賊預焚草地，我軍紆道秣馬。

translations.literal: Heavy rains delayed grain transport; the enemy had beforehand burned the grasslands; our army took detours to graze the horses.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains delayed supplies; the enemy had burned the pastures ahead, forcing our army to detour to feed the horses.

sentences.zh: 音泰言於博霽曰：「聖駕親征，宜倍道前進。

translations.literal: Yin Tai said to Bo Ji: "With the Sacred Majesty campaigning in person, we should march at double speed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Tai told Bo Ji: "With the emperor campaigning in person, we should march at forced pace.

sentences.zh: 」乃急趨昭莫多，大軍繼進，噶爾丹敗遁。

translations.literal: " They then rushed toward Jao Modo; the main army followed; Galdan was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: " They rushed to Jao Modo; the main army followed; Galdan was routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 敘功，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed he was granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，遷佐領。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he was transferred to assistant battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year he was promoted to assistant battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，上巡西安，令官兵校射，音泰蒙賚與賜宴，尋授協領。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year the emperor toured Xi'an, ordered officers and soldiers to compete in archery; Yin Tai received imperial gifts and was granted a banquet, and soon afterward was appointed deputy battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year, during the imperial tour of Xi'an, Yin Tai distinguished himself in the archery competition, received gifts and a banquet, and was soon made deputy battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，擢西安副都統。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was promoted to Xi'an lieutenant-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he was promoted to lieutenant-general of Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，授西寧總兵官。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was appointed regional commander of Xining.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year he became regional commander of Xining.

sentences.zh: 上知其貧，詔陝西督撫助練兵犒賚之資。

translations.literal: The emperor knew he was poor and ordered the governor and governor-general of Shaanxi to assist with funds for training troops and bestowing rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he was poor, the emperor ordered Shaanxi's governor and governor-general to help fund troop training and rewards.

sentences.zh: 四十六年諭：「音泰久居西陲，諳習兵事，外籓蒙古及內地軍民交口稱譽。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year an edict stated: "Yin Tai has long dwelt on the western frontier, is thoroughly versed in military affairs, and is praised alike by outer Mongol tribes and inner military and civilian alike.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year an edict declared: "Yin Tai has long served on the western frontier, knows military affairs well, and is praised by Mongol frontier tribes and Han civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 」命擢甘肅提督。

translations.literal: " He was ordered promoted to military commander of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to military commander of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，授川陝總督。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he was appointed governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he was made governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 入覲，賞花翎及冠服、鞍馬，並御書「攬轡澄清」榜賜之。

translations.literal: Upon attending audience he was rewarded with a peacock feather, court dress, saddle and horse, and also granted a plaque bearing the imperial inscription "Gathering the Reins to Clear the Mire."
translations.idiomatic: At court he received a peacock feather, ceremonial robes, a saddle and horse, and an imperial plaque inscribed "Gathering the Reins to Clear the Mire"—a summons to take office with clean purpose.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，幹偉番蠻羅都等掠寧番衛，戕冕山營游擊周玉麟，命四川巡撫年羹堯偕提督岳昇龍往剿。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year Ganwei fan barbarians Luo Du and others raided Ningfan Guard, killed Yingshan Camp brigade commander Zhou Yulin, and the court ordered Sichuan governor Nian Gengyao together with military commander Yue Shenglong to go suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year Luo Du and other Ganwei tribesmen raided Ningfan Guard and killed brigade commander Zhou Yulin of Yingshan Camp; the court sent Sichuan governor Nian Gengyao and military commander Yue Shenglong to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 羹堯至，昇龍已擒羅都等三人械送勘問。

translations.literal: When Gengyao arrived, Shenglong had already captured Luo Du and three others, sent them bound for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Nian Gengyao arrived, Yue Shenglong had already captured Luo Du and two others and sent them bound for trial.

sentences.zh: 既定讞，遂先還。

translations.literal: Once the case was decided, he then returned first.
translations.idiomatic: After the verdict was settled, he returned ahead of the others.

sentences.zh: 昇龍偕建昌總兵郝弘勳至會鹽招降，番蠻諸酋原率眾十萬貢納糧馬。

translations.literal: Shenglong together with Jianchang regional commander Hao Hongxun reached Huiyan to accept surrender; various fan barbarian chieftains, Yuan leading, brought a host of one hundred thousand to present tribute of grain and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Shenglong and Jianchang regional commander Hao Hongxun went to Huiyan to accept surrenders; chieftain Yuan and other tribal leaders brought a hundred thousand followers to submit grain and horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 音泰請以降酋為土司，分領其眾。

translations.literal: Yin Tai requested that the surrendered chieftains be made native chieftains to divide rule over their followers.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Tai proposed appointing the surrendered chieftains as native rulers, each to govern his own followers.

sentences.zh: 因劾羹堯違旨先還，詔奪羹堯職，留任效力。

translations.literal: Because he impeached Gengyao for violating orders by returning first, an edict stripped Gengyao of his post but kept him in office to serve effectively.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Nian Gengyao for disobeying orders by returning early; the emperor stripped Gengyao of his rank but allowed him to remain and serve.

sentences.zh: 未幾，昇龍以疾解任，羹堯知其曾假帑金，議率屬捐俸代償，音泰不從。

translations.literal: Before long Shenglong resigned due to illness; Gengyao knew he had once borrowed treasury funds and proposed that subordinates donate salaries to repay on his behalf; Yin Tai refused.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yue Shenglong resigned for illness; learning he had once borrowed public funds, Nian Gengyao proposed that officials donate salary to repay the debt, but Yin Tai refused.

sentences.zh: 羹堯遂入告，上允行，並諭音泰宜與巡撫和衷。

translations.literal: Gengyao then reported to the throne; the emperor approved the plan and also instructed Yin Tai that he should harmonize with the governor.
translations.idiomatic: Nian Gengyao reported to the emperor, who approved the repayment scheme and urged Yin Tai to work in harmony with the governor.

sentences.zh: 尋褒其潔清不瞻徇，實心任事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was praised for integrity without favoritism and for serving conscientiously.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon commended his incorruptibility and impartial, conscientious service.

sentences.zh: 會奉詔申禁遊民越境，令嚴劾縱容官吏。

translations.literal: At this time he received an edict reiterating the ban on vagrants crossing borders and ordering strict impeachment of officials who indulged them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict arrived reiterating the ban on migrant vagrants crossing provincial boundaries and demanding strict punishment of lax officials.

sentences.zh: 邠州諸屬拘系者四十餘案，每案至數十人。

translations.literal: In various subordinate districts of Binzhou over forty cases had been detained, each case involving as many as several dozen persons.
translations.idiomatic: In Binzhou and its subordinate districts more than forty cases had been opened, some involving dozens of detainees each.

sentences.zh: 音泰疏言諸人皆藉技營生，無不法狀，應遞解原籍編管；

translations.literal: Yin Tai memorialized that all these persons made their living by skills, had no unlawful conduct, and should be escorted back to their native places for registration and supervision;
translations.idiomatic: Yin Tai reported that the detainees were skilled laborers earning honest livings with no criminal record and should be returned to their home districts for registration and supervision;

sentences.zh: 如縱出境，議處所司，上韙之。

translations.literal: If officials allowed them to leave the jurisdiction, the responsible offices should be held accountable; the emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who let such persons cross borders should be punished; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 以病疏乞休，上曰：「朕前幸西安，知音泰義勇，洊擢至總督。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he memorialized requesting retirement; the emperor said: "When I previously visited Xi'an I knew Yin Tai's courage and loyalty and repeatedly promoted him to governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to retire on grounds of illness; the emperor replied: "On my tour of Xi'an I recognized Yin Tai's courage and loyalty and raised him step by step to governor-general.

sentences.zh: 寬嚴並用，軍民無不感戴。

translations.literal: Using lenience and severity together, military and civilian alike were all grateful.
translations.idiomatic: His blend of lenience and severity won the gratitude of soldiers and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 朕甚愛惜之，可令在任調攝。

translations.literal: I cherish him greatly; he may remain in office under leave to recuperate.
translations.idiomatic: I value him highly; let him remain in office while taking time to recover.

sentences.zh: 」五十二年，復請，許解任還京師，給第宅田畝，以旌其廉。

translations.literal: " In the fifty-second year he requested again; he was permitted to leave his post and return to the capital, granted a residence and fields in recognition of his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifty-second year he petitioned again; the emperor allowed him to retire to the capital and granted him a residence and farmland in honor of his integrity.

sentences.zh: 並諭群臣曰：「朕初用音泰，人不知其善，後乃稱朕有知人之明也。

translations.literal: He also told the assembled ministers: "When I first employed Yin Tai people did not know his worth; afterward they praised my discernment in knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: He told his ministers: "When I first appointed Yin Tai, few recognized his talent; later all praised my judgment in choosing men.

sentences.zh: 」五十三年，卒，賜祭葬，諡清端。

translations.literal: " In the fifty-third year he died; funeral rites were granted and he was posthumously titled Qingduan ("Pure and Upright").
translations.idiomatic: " He died in the fifty-third year; the court granted funeral honors and posthumously named him Qingduan, "Pure and Upright."

sentences.zh: 初授雲騎尉世職，特命世襲罔替。

translations.literal: Initially granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Commandant, he was specially ordered that the inheritance continue in perpetuity without demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Though first granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Commandant, he was specially granted perpetual inheritance without reduction of rank.

sentences.zh: 鄂海，溫都氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: E Hai, of the Wensu clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: E Hai, of the Wensu clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 自筆帖式授內閣中書，歷宗人府郎中，兼佐領。

translations.literal: From clerk of the Grand Secretariat he was appointed Grand Secretariat secretary, served as director in the Imperial Clan Court, and concurrently held assistant battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a Grand Secretariat clerk, he became a secretariat secretary, served as a director in the Imperial Clan Court, and concurrently held assistant battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十二年，聖祖親征噶爾丹，命鄂海赴寧夏儲備牲畜。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi the Sacred Ancestor personally campaigned against Galdan and ordered E Hai to go to Ningxia to stockpile livestock.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 32 the emperor personally campaigned against Galdan and sent E Hai to Ningxia to gather livestock.

sentences.zh: 陝西按察使員缺，上以命鄂海，且諭之曰：「初任外僚，每言潔其身以圖報。

translations.literal: With the Shaanxi provincial surveillance commissioner post vacant, the emperor appointed E Hai and instructed him: "On first taking provincial office one always speaks of keeping oneself pure to repay the court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shaanxi surveillance commissioner post fell vacant, the emperor appointed E Hai with these words: "New provincial officials always vow to keep themselves clean in repayment of imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 及蒞任，輒背其言。

translations.literal: Yet once they assume office they invariably go back on their words.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once in office they invariably break that promise.

sentences.zh: 朕於數十從臣中簡爾為按察使，爾當益勵素行也。

translations.literal: I have selected you from among dozens of attendants as surveillance commissioner; you should all the more encourage your accustomed conduct.
translations.idiomatic: I have chosen you from among dozens of courtiers for this post; see that you live up to the character you have shown.

sentences.zh: 」三十七年，遷布政使。

translations.literal: " In the thirty-seventh year he was transferred to provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: " In the thirty-seventh year he was promoted to provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四十年，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he became governor.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，授湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he was appointed governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year he was made governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 鎮筸邊外紅苗為亂，令總兵張谷貞等召苗目宣諭，毛都塘等五十二寨、盤塘等八十三寨，先後薙發歸化，上嘉之。

translations.literal: Red Miao beyond the Zhenqian border stirred rebellion; he ordered regional commander Zhang Guzhen and others to summon Miao headmen for proclamation; fifty-two stockades including Maodutang and eighty-three including Pantang successively shaved their heads and submitted; the emperor commended this.
translations.idiomatic: When Red Miao beyond the Zhenqian frontier rebelled, he sent regional commander Zhang Guzhen to summon tribal headmen; fifty-two stockades including Maodutang and eighty-three including Pantang successively tonsured and submitted; the emperor praised the result.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，移督川、陝。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was transferred to govern Sichuan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year he was transferred to governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 疏報甘肅洮、岷邊外大山生番請歸化，上以洮、岷邊外無生番，或為蒙古屬部，命詳察。

translations.literal: He reported that raw tribes beyond the Tao and Min borders in Gansu requested submission; the emperor held that there were no raw tribes beyond Tao and Min, that they might be Mongol dependent tribes, and ordered thorough investigation.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that wild tribes beyond the Tao and Min frontier in Gansu sought to submit; the emperor noted that no such tribes existed there and that they might be Mongol dependents, and ordered a full inquiry.

sentences.zh: 鄂海奏大山在洮州東南土司楊汝松界外，非蒙古屬部，宜令汝松兼轄；

translations.literal: E Hai memorialized that Dashan lay beyond the boundary of native chieftain Yang Rusong southeast of Taozhou, was not a Mongol dependent tribe, and Yang Rusong should be ordered to govern it as well;
translations.idiomatic: E Hai reported that Dashan lay outside the jurisdiction of native chieftain Yang Rusong southeast of Taozhou, was not a Mongol dependency, and should be placed under Yang's expanded authority;

sentences.zh: 复疏報四川會川營界外涼山番目阿木哨請歸化，歲貢馬，請給番目職銜，令轄所屬番、民：並從之。

translations.literal: He again reported that Liangshan fan headman Amushao beyond the Huichuan Camp boundary in Sichuan requested submission, offered annual tribute of horses, and requested a fan headman title to govern his subordinate fan and civilian populations: all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that tribal headman Amushao of Liangshan beyond the Huichuan garrison in Sichuan sought submission, offered horses as annual tribute, and requested an official title to govern his people; the court approved all requests.

sentences.zh: 甘肅靖遠、固原、會寧歲歉飢，民乏食，疏給口糧資本，撫輯流移。

translations.literal: In Jingyuan, Guyuan, and Huining in Gansu years of poor harvest brought famine and the people lacked food; he memorialized to grant subsistence grain and seed capital and to pacify displaced migrants.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Jingyuan, Guyuan, and Huining in Gansu, he distributed grain and seed funds and worked to settle displaced refugees.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，大將軍貝子允等率師討策妄阿喇布坦，駐兵西寧、甘州、莊浪諸處。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year Grand General Prince Yin and others led troops to campaign against Tsewang Rabtan, stationing forces at Xining, Ganzhou, Zhuanglang, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year Grand General Prince Yin marched against Tsewang Rabtan, quartering troops at Xining, Ganzhou, Zhuanglang, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 鄂海請發西安庫帑四十萬，並撥平涼、鞏昌、寧夏倉穀十萬，充餉；

translations.literal: E Hai requested disbursing four hundred thousand taels from the Xi'an treasury and allocating one hundred thousand piculs of grain from storehouses at Pingliang, Gongchang, and Ningxia for rations;
translations.idiomatic: E Hai requested four hundred thousand taels from the Xi'an treasury and a hundred thousand piculs of grain from stores at Pingliang, Gongchang, and Ningxia for army rations;

sentences.zh: 以陝西葭州、甘肅寧夏等二十八處轉輸軍需，請豁丁糧，紓民力。

translations.literal: Because twenty-eight places including Jiazhou in Shaanxi and Ningxia in Gansu transported military supplies, he requested exemption from labor grain levies to ease the people's burden.
translations.idiomatic: With twenty-eight relay points including Jiazhou in Shaanxi and Ningxia in Gansu moving supplies, he asked to exempt labor grain levies to ease the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，復請豁甘肅逋欠錢糧草束，俾民得盡力輸納本年糧草以佐軍，戶部格不行，特旨允之。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he again requested remitting Gansu's arrears in money, grain, and fodder so the people could devote their strength to paying current year's grain and fodder to support the army; the Board of Revenue blocked it but a special edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year he again sought remission of Gansu's arrears in taxes, grain, and fodder so people could pay the current year's levies for the campaign; the Board of Revenue refused, but the emperor overruled and granted it.

sentences.zh: 六十年，詔解任專治糧餉，以四川巡撫年羹堯代之。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year an edict relieved him of general duties to specialize in managing grain rations, with Sichuan governor Nian Gengyao replacing him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he was relieved of general duties to focus solely on supplies, with Sichuan governor Nian Gengyao succeeding to his broader post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，命往吐魯番種地效力。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered to go to Turfan to farm and serve effectively.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent to Turfan to serve through agricultural labor.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，予原品休致，效力如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was granted retirement at his original rank while continuing to serve as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he was permitted to retire at his former rank while continuing his assigned service.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 衛既齊，字伯嚴，山西猗氏人。

translations.literal: Wei Jiqi, courtesy name Boyan, was a native of Yishi, Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiqi, styled Boyan, was from Yishi in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 父紹芳，字猶箴，順治三年進士，授河南尉氏知縣。

translations.literal: His father Shaofang, courtesy name Youzhen, a jinshi of the third year of Shunzhi, was appointed magistrate of Weishi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaofang, styled Youzhen, passed the jinshi examination in Shunzhi 3 and became magistrate of Weishi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 兵後修復城郭、學校，勤勸課，廣積儲，禁暴戢姦，尉氏民頌焉。

translations.literal: After the wars he repaired walls and schools, diligently encouraged agriculture, broadly accumulated stores, suppressed violence and quelled crime; the people of Weishi praised him.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars he rebuilt walls and schools, promoted farming, built up reserves, and suppressed crime; the people of Weishi praised him.

sentences.zh: 行取兵部主事，累遷貴州提學道僉事、浙江巡海道副使。

translations.literal: Selected for service he became a secretary in the Ministry of War, and through successive promotions became judicial commissioner of the Guizhou education circuit and vice commissioner of the Zhejiang coastal defense circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from the ranks, he served as a secretary in the Ministry of War, then rose to education intendant in Guizhou and vice commissioner of Zhejiang coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 既齊，康熙三年進士，改庶吉士，散館授檢討。

translations.literal: Jiqi, a jinshi of the third year of Kangxi, was changed to Hanlin bachelor; upon leaving the Hanlin Academy he was appointed reviewing compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiqi passed the jinshi in Kangxi 3, entered the Hanlin Academy, and upon graduation was appointed reviewing compiler.

sentences.zh: 講學志當世之務，上疏言時事，語戇直。

translations.literal: Lecturing on learning he aimed at the tasks of the age; he memorialized on current affairs in blunt, straight language.
translations.idiomatic: In his lectures he addressed the pressing issues of the day; his memorials on current affairs were blunt and forthright.

sentences.zh: 會遭祖母喪，假歸。

translations.literal: He happened to suffer his grandmother's death and took leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandmother died he took leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 居久之，詣京師補官。

translations.literal: After dwelling long at home he went to the capital to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: After a long stay at home he returned to the capital to resume his post.

sentences.zh: 上命以對品調外，授直隸霸州州判。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him transferred outside at equivalent rank and appointed judge of Bazhou in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor transferred him to an outside post at equivalent rank, appointing him assistant magistrate of Bazhou in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 既齊召民之秀良者曹試而教誨之，俾各有所成就。

translations.literal: Jiqi summoned the outstanding and good among the people, tested them in groups, and instructed them so that each might achieve in his way.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the county's promising young men, examined them in groups, and tutored them so each could develop his talents.

sentences.zh: 民貸於旗丁，子錢過倍，橫索無已。

translations.literal: Civilians borrowed from banner soldiers; interest exceeded double the principal and extortion never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Civilians who borrowed from bannermen faced interest above double the principal and endless harassment.

sentences.zh: 既齊力禁戢之，無敢逞。

translations.literal: Jiqi vigorously forbade and suppressed this; none dared act arrogantly.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiqi rigorously suppressed the practice until no one dared abuse it.

sentences.zh: 迭署固安、永清、平谷知縣，所至輒有惠政。

translations.literal: He served in succession as acting magistrate of Gu'an, Yongqing, and Pinggu; wherever he went he promptly had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Serving in turn as acting magistrate of Gu'an, Yongqing, and Pinggu, he left benevolent policies wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 巡撫於成龍疏薦。

translations.literal: Governor Yu Chenglong memorialized recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yu Chenglong recommended him in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 會既齊以母憂去，繼复遭父喪。

translations.literal: As Jiqi was leaving on account of his mother's mourning, he subsequently also suffered his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Jiqi left office for his mother's mourning, his father also died soon after.

sentences.zh: 一日，上御門，舉既齊諮於九卿，僉曰賢，命复授檢討。

translations.literal: One day the emperor held court, raised Jiqi for consultation with the Nine Ministers; all said he was worthy and he was ordered again appointed reviewing compiler.
translations.idiomatic: One day at imperial audience the emperor asked the Nine Ministers about Wei Jiqi; all declared him worthy, and he was reappointed reviewing compiler.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，服闋，詣京師補官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, when mourning closed, he went to the capital to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, when his mourning period ended, he returned to the capital to resume service.

sentences.zh: 上知既齊講學負清望，超擢山東布政使。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Jiqi's lectures and clean reputation and extraordinarily promoted him to Shandong provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Wei Jiqi's scholarly reputation and integrity, the emperor bypassed normal promotion and made him Shandong provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既齊感激，益自奮勉為清廉，令府縣輸款封還平餘。

translations.literal: Jiqi was grateful and all the more exerted himself in integrity; he ordered prefectures and counties to remit funds and return sealed surpluses.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for the trust, he doubled his efforts at integrity, ordering prefectures and counties to remit revenues and return any surplus intact.

sentences.zh: 門懸鉦，吏民白事得自通。

translations.literal: A gong was hung at his gate; clerks and people reporting matters could reach him directly.
translations.idiomatic: He hung a gong at his gate so officials and commoners could petition him directly.

sentences.zh: 建歷山書院，仿經義、治事之例，設奎、壁二齋課士。

translations.literal: He built Lishan Academy, following the models of "Classics" and "Practical Affairs," establishing the Kui and Bi studios to examine scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He founded Lishan Academy with Kui and Bi halls, modeled on the Hanlin categories of classical learning and practical governance, to instruct scholars.

sentences.zh: 護巡撫印者再。

translations.literal: He twice held the governor's seal in guardianship.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 清庶獄，結八十餘案，株累數百人盡釋去。

translations.literal: He cleared accumulated cases, concluding over eighty cases and releasing several hundred persons implicated by association.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared the backlog of cases, closing more than eighty proceedings and releasing hundreds who had been implicated by association.

sentences.zh: 在官三年，有聲績。

translations.literal: During three years in office he had reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In three years in office he won distinction.

sentences.zh: 三十年，授順天府尹，疏請按行所部，黜陟屬吏賢不肖。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was appointed metropolitan governor of Shuntian and memorialized requesting to tour his jurisdiction to promote and dismiss subordinate officials according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he became metropolitan governor of Shuntian and asked to tour his district to promote worthy subordinates and remove the unfit.

sentences.zh: 上以為無益，不許。

translations.literal: The emperor considered this without benefit and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw no benefit in the proposal and refused.

sentences.zh: 尋擢副都御史，聞山、陝蝗見，平陽以南尤甚，疏請賑恤，上責其懸揣。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief; hearing locusts appeared in Shanxi and Shaanxi, especially severe south of Pingyang, he memorialized requesting relief; the emperor rebuked him for presumption.
translations.idiomatic: Soon promoted to vice censor-in-chief, he heard of locusts in Shanxi and Shaanxi, worst south of Pingyang, and memorialized for relief; the emperor rebuked him for speculating without evidence.

sentences.zh: 旋授貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 紹芳為提學，士民祠焉。

translations.literal: Shaofang had served as education intendant and gentry and people erected a shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaofang had served as education intendant, and scholars and commoners had built a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 既齊至貴州，謁父祠受事。

translations.literal: When Jiqi reached Guizhou he visited his father's shrine before taking up duties.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Guizhou, Wei Jiqi visited his father's shrine before assuming office.

sentences.zh: 黎平知府張瀲、副將侯奇嵩報古州高洞苗金濤匿罪人殺吏，請發兵進剿，既齊疏聞，即遣兵捕治；

translations.literal: Liping prefect Zhang Lian and vice-general Hou Qisong reported that Gaodong Miao Jin Tao of Guzhou harbored criminals and killed officials, requesting troops for a punitive advance; Jiqi reported this and immediately sent troops to capture and punish;
translations.idiomatic: Liping prefect Zhang Lian and vice-general Hou Qisong reported that Jin Tao, a Gaodong Miao of Guzhou, was harboring criminals and had killed officials, and asked for a punitive expedition; Wei Jiqi reported this at once and dispatched troops;

sentences.zh: 瀲、奇嵩复報兵至斬苗一千一百一十八人，既齊復以聞。

translations.literal: Lian and Qisong again reported that upon troops' arrival one thousand one hundred eighteen Miao were beheaded; Jiqi again reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lian and Hou Qisong then reported that the troops had beheaded 1,118 Miao; Wei Jiqi relayed this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 旋察知瀲、奇嵩妄報，疏實陳，請奪瀲、奇嵩官勘治。

translations.literal: Soon learning that Lian and Qisong had falsely reported, he memorialized stating the facts and requesting deprivation of Lian and Qisong's offices for investigation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the report was false, he submitted the facts and asked that Zhang Lian and Hou Qisong be stripped of rank and investigated.

sentences.zh: 上責既齊輕率虛妄，遣尚書庫勒納、內閣學士溫保往按。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Jiqi for rashness and falsehood and dispatched Minister Kule Na and Grand Secretariat academician Wen Bao to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed Wei Jiqi for reckless credulity and sent Minister Kule Na and Grand Secretariat academician Wen Bao to investigate.

sentences.zh: 旋命逮既齊至京師，上令九卿詰責。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to escort Jiqi to the capital; the emperor had the Nine Ministers interrogate and rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiqi was soon summoned to the capital, where the Nine Ministers interrogated him on the emperor's orders.

sentences.zh: 既齊引罪請死，九卿議當斬，上命貸之，遣戍黑龍江。

translations.literal: Jiqi accepted guilt and requested death; the Nine Ministers adjudged decapitation warranted; the emperor ordered sparing him and sent him to exile in Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiqi accepted blame and asked for death; the Nine Ministers recommended execution; the emperor spared him and exiled him to Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 明年，赦還。

translations.literal: The next year he was pardoned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was pardoned and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 家居，立社課士，斥家資供膏火。

translations.literal: Living at home he established a society to examine scholars and spent family wealth to supply lamp oil and ink.
translations.idiomatic: At home he founded a literary society, spending his own fortune on students' supplies.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，上命承修永定河工。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year the emperor ordered him to undertake repair of the Yongding River works.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year the emperor put him in charge of Yongding River repairs.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，又命督培高家堰，卒工次。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was again ordered to supervise strengthening of the Gaojiayan embankment and died at the works.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he was assigned to reinforce the Gaojiayan embankment and died on the job.

sentences.zh: 論曰：康熙中葉後，天下乂安，封疆大吏多尚廉能，奉職循理。

translations.literal: The commentator says: After the middle of Kangxi, under heaven all was tranquil; frontier great officials mostly valued integrity and ability and fulfilled duties according to principle.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: After the mid-Kangxi era the empire was at peace, and frontier governors mostly prized integrity and competence, fulfilling their duties conscientiously.

sentences.zh: 若石琳改賦役，徐潮革火耗，博霽、華​​顯、音泰整飭武備，安不忘危，皆能舉其職者。

translations.literal: Such as Shi Lin reforming taxes and corvée, Xu Chao abolishing meltage fees, Bo Ji, Hua Xian, and Yin Tai rectifying military preparedness—secure yet not forgetting danger—all were able to fulfill their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Lin reformed tax and corvée assessments, Xu Chao abolished meltage surcharges, and Bo Ji, Hua Xian, and Yin Tai strengthened military readiness—secure yet vigilant—all fulfilling their duties well.

sentences.zh: 劉廕樞志在休民，未知應兵之不容已，蔣陳錫、鄂海又以督餉稽遲蒙譴，衛既齊遭際殊異，而不獲以功名終，其治行皆有可稱，膏澤及於民，無深淺遠近，要為不沫矣。

translations.literal: Liu Yinshu aspired to rest the people yet did not know that military response could not be avoided; Jiang Chenxi and E Hai also suffered censure for delay in supervising grain rations; Wei Jiqi encountered singular circumstances and did not obtain to end in fame and achievement—yet their governance all had points worth praise; their bounty reached the people without regard to depth, nearness, or distance—in essence undimmed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yinshu sought to give the people rest but failed to see that war could not always be avoided; Jiang Chenxi and E Hai were censured for supply delays; Wei Jiqi's fate was singular and he did not finish his career in glory—yet all had governance worth praise; their benefits reached the people alike, near or far, great or small—in the end their legacy has not faded.
